And whatever they may scream at you, don't park your bike until you get inside the ticket gate. Why walk more than you have to?

reviews.author: TIT Adventure
reviews.title: Trang An boat trip and Mua viewpoint
reviews.content: a wonderful day trip from Hanoi to Hang Mua viewpoint & Trang An landscape with lovely team from Emirate organised by TÍT Adventure

reviews.author: Hetzel
reviews.title: Climbing up is the highlight
reviews.content: It was a great thing to do, is less challenging than I expected,,, the view from the top is actually so nice, I found it a bit confusing that the place is marketed as Mua Caves, however , in my personal experience, the caves aren't impressive, but the climb to the top of the mountain with the steps is a nice experience.I didn't do a tour, just went by cab with my friends. Use meter, don't accept price offer.Taxi driver will offer to wait for you to take you wherever else you are going. You can accept that, but again, with meter (meaning he will stop the meter when you arrive there, and restart it when you come back, is his choice to wait for you.I highly recommend to be there at 7 am as it just opens, temperature is nice and less exhausting, very little people...( only thing is that the little shops or stands are closed to buy drinks or so, but you are not missing out) much better barely any people...nice to go at your own pace and take pictures easily.If you have bad knees, or are very overweight, this is maybe not a good option to do.

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: What a view
reviews.content: We had a guide drop us here, so did not have to battle with the parking touts, which made our life easier.  Take your time hear and wear comfy shoes as the stairs are very steep and slippery in places.  Some steps are very high for little legs.  Its not a race to the top, stop and look around and enjoy the views, they are stunning.  May not be worth doing on a really overcast day as you wont see a great deal.  My family enjoyed this and you come to a fork in the path - left to the dragon and view of rowers in Tam Coc and we decided to do both.  There is a place to get a cold drink half way up which is really nice, they have a seat with a fan set up for the hot sticky days.  There is also places to get cold drinks and ice-cream at the bottom.  Be very careful with young children as not a lot of safety rails, but common sense applies.  Well worth the trip to the top, the views are stunning.

reviews.author: TheGrebes
reviews.title: Lovely climb and views ... Very persistent parking touts
reviews.content: Great experience. Stunning views, but a very steep climb. Relatively quiet when we were there but could be a bit dangerous if crowded as steps very steep and narrow in p!aces. A few people blocking parts of the climb getting their breath back quite awkward to safely manouver around.The parking scam is very evident and even knowing about it we still got caught out by an official looking guy in a u inform of some kind right at the entrance gate. The official parking (cycles and scooters) is inside the gate behind the ticket office. Just say NO loudly to all the touts that try to stop you on the road approaching the gate.

reviews.author: ctm7944
reviews.title: Hang Mua - Wow The Views!
reviews.content: Rode FREE bicycle from accommodations (Tam Coc Wonderland Bungalows). Arrived Hang Mua about 10AM (Open 6AM-7PM).Couldn't have picked a better day to have some morning sunshine. Yes, it is 500 steps. Some of the many stone steps are quite high. But, I enjoyed the challenge/exercise. Eventually you come to a fork in the road. The path to the Left goes up to the highest point (dragon). On this path is where you see the Tam Coc boats passing on the water below. This being the higher path, you can also get great photos of the Pagoda + the countryside.The Right side path leads to the Pagoda with nice views as well.Yes, the RICE fields are GREEN in April.And of course there were lots of tourists there; doing tourist things - just like me.Hang Mua entry is 100KVND. Bicycle parking 10VND.Previous TA reviews were helpful. Advised to ignore people waving me to parking. Some stand in the road and a few had on uniforms to appear as some type of official.Parked at the lot at the end of the road (on the right side), which is immediately before the ticket office.Took photos along the way to & from; people working the fields, buffalo and limestone formations etc. Very scenic!

reviews.author: mabellan
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: Great views. I couldn’t see a good sunset as there was a bit misty but it was totally worth it. The mountain opposite was less crowded and had a few less steps but we decided to do Mua anyway. Best in mind that you need to get a ticket and it’s cash only

reviews.author: Jaroslav Nečas
reviews.title: Spectacular views
reviews.content: To see fantastic views you need to walk up several hundreds steep stairs but it's definitely worth it. There are 2 peaks, higher is more crowded lesser not so much. You probably would need to wait some time to get position for good photo.

reviews.author: Thuy
reviews.title: Hang Mua should be in favorite list if you travel to Ninh Binh
reviews.content: This is nice place to see almost of Tam Coc from the top. Also is natural place for travelers can take photos to save memories

reviews.author: Kelly B
reviews.title: Beautiful viewpoint, but be aware of aggression and scams
reviews.content: The viewpoint is stunning and well worth the short climb (15 mins if you are reasonably fit) but as other reviewers have said, it's important to know what to expect regarding the parking scams on the entrance road.I had several people jump in front of my bike trying to force me to stop before the entrance gate, a woman grabbed my arm as I cycled past her and tried to pull me off my bike, and eventually ended up with 5 men surrounding my bike, screaming at me and kicking my bike very aggressively while I was still sitting on it. As a woman on my own it was intimidating and I ended up parking in their area just to diffuse the situation as I was worried they were about to hit me. Even though I was expecting some of this behaviour (from reading other reviews), I was scared and quite shaken by how furious the men were and how unsafe they made me feel.  Don't let this put you off visiting the beautiful viewpoint - but be prepared for some aggression and go with a friend for extra safety if you can.

reviews.author: must_travel_soon_10
reviews.title: Majestic views are worth climbing the steps
reviews.content: There are approx. 500 steps and they lead to beautiful vistas of the surrounding areas with limestone peaks. We went mid afternoon and didn't encounter excessive crowds. The base area is also very scenic and beautiful. One of three must sees in Ninh Binh

reviews.author: Allison G
reviews.title: Beautiful viewpoint worth the stairs
reviews.content: Great view point worth the stairs. Very hot so bring water. There’s a scam with a man and woman with a whistle who will try to get you to park your scooter or bike and pay for parking (do not do this). Go straight to the ticket counter!

reviews.author: Madiyya
reviews.title: A place to escape the hustle and bustle of Hanoi
reviews.content: This hidden gem offers stunning views of the limestone mountains and rice fields, as well as a chance to explore the mysterious caves that lie beneath. You'll need to climb 500 steps to reach the top of the mountain, but trust me, it's worth it. The view from the peak is breathtaking, especially at sunset. You'll feel like you're in a fairy tale.

reviews.author: Romain H
reviews.title: Parking scam
reviews.content: Do not park outside it’s a scam! Park inside the gate (to the left side after the entrance)5000 VND for bike 10.000 VND for motorbike

reviews.author: Marta R
reviews.title: Worth every step!
reviews.content: We rode a scooter out in the morning. Had read earlier reviews about the parking scam but didn’t find it to be an issue this morning. There was a woman trying to wave us down, but we were able to ride past her easily.There are shops selling dresses on the street as you lead in. Wish I had taken a bit more notice as it’s traditional dress that you can wear up the steps and take some beautiful photos in. It’s only about 600,00 Duong for the dresses so if you want something extra special for your photo have a look at them. Definitely Instagram worthy. Yes there are about 1000 steps and everyone of them is worth it. Due to the beautiful nature you stop every 20-40 steps to take photos and take it all in so you don’t feel completely out of breath (a little sweaty depending on the temperature).The view at the top is magnificent and worth the effort. The dragon is not all that accessible but the view is still spectacular.

reviews.author: majorstu
reviews.title: Beautiful views - definitely a must do when in the area
reviews.content: Our family of 5 ( 2 adults, 3 kids - 14. 11, 8) biked from Tam Coc - a pretty steady flat ride.  Be prepared for the parking fee - a slightly irritating common feature in the area at most attractions, followed by your entrance fee.  I’ve read the parking hassle other reviewers had - we just bypassed the early offerings and parked right outside the entrance gate and paid up.  The caves were OK (nothing compared to those experienced on the Trang An boat tour), but the viewpoint makes it, with beautiful views across the lush rice paddies, waterways and towering limestone cliffs.  As in many places rubbish is a sad accompaniment as is poor maintenance, but  the view really showcases the beauty of the area.  If you’ve got reasonable fitness climbing the 500 steps takes about 15-20 minutes.

reviews.author: Leannie
reviews.title: Worth the steps
reviews.content: Came here as a family of four, and as we arrived by car we did not get any of the hassle described by previous reviewers arriving by car. Once you have paid and entered there are some nice viewing seats/swings with good views, as well as bathrooms which are fine if you bring your own toilet roll.  We started the climb to the viewing point about 4.30m, it was not too busy, we liked the fact that the stairs were very wide allowing two way traffic without it being too busy. I appreciated the many stop points on the way up for breath and taking photos. Didn't make it right to the top, but seeing as I was q hot mess by that point and have no intracranial account to add photos too that was just fine

reviews.author: Christelle Z
reviews.title: Agressive and violent people for parking in front
reviews.content: Very nice view but scam at the entrance on the price of parking.  2 people in fake police ask 10k VND to park motorbike/bicycle.  I refused to pay as I knew there was official parking inside.  One of the two people attacked me, he became violent and kicked my bike 3 times.  I also specify that they looked clearly in a state of intoxication, they were drinking in front of the entrance.  One of the two then wanted to hit me but the park staff intervened.  He then insulted me in Vietnamese and I ended up parking my bike in the official parking lot for 5k VND. On the other hand, no one came to help me afterwards to call the police, the park staff did not want to get involved because they were afraid of reprisals;  and when I finally found the number of the police they told me that they could not come and that I had to go to the station. Really a shame because the point of view is exceptional, but to fear for her safety in Vietnam (especially as a woman) - I pass my turn. Knowing economy relies on tourism, I don’t understand how the police doesn’t take care of this issue, it really stains my memory of Vietnam

reviews.author: Yann Renaud
reviews.title: Breathtaking sceneries
reviews.content: Definitely a place to visit when in the area. From Tam Coc, the place is easily accessible.on bike or motorbike. When arriving, many people try to stop you in order for you to park at their place. The further you can go with your bike/motorbike, is just before the gate before the ticket office. The parking.spot.costs between 10-15kD.The entrance costs 100kD/person, and it is absolutely worth it! You will have to climb around 500 uneven stairs, made of a slippery rock. At a given point you can turn left and reach the top, with the Dragon and a wonderful view over Tam Coc, or right and have another impressive view.

reviews.author: Davina M
reviews.title: READ THE ONE STAR REVIEWS- DANGEROUS! AVOID!
reviews.content: When driving up towards the entrance, locals literally stand in front of out motorbikes and forcefully tried to stop us to pay for parking. We kept swerving around them, as we knew that it was free parking through the gate. At the entrance to buy the tickets, there were two men, very aggressive, who stopped us and were screaming at us that we couldn't go through the gate to park and we had to pay them. Having been in South East Asia for a while we know not to get angry and were calmly saying to them we are going through the gate, it's free parking. They physically would not let us and the older man became so aggressive he got right in front of my face and appeared like he was ready to punch me in the face. My boyfriend got off his bike and walked through the gate to talk to the kiosk for tickets and for them to let us through. While this was happening, the same guy who I thought was going to hit me, grabbed a large metal chain and was swinging it at my boyfriends motorbike and looked like he intended to hit it and lock it up. I started yelling at him to back off, which he did before starting to get back in my face yelling. The ticket people didn't care and were super apathetic. We decided to leave, I didn't want to support people  who were so violent. Before you go here - read the one star reviews from 2019. There is a photo of the same bloke and other foreigners who did get hit, threatened with the chain and knives.

reviews.author: Elisabeth N
reviews.title: Taxing climb for the unfit, but the top is worth the sweat
reviews.content: Over 400 steps, some .5m high!!! This is not an easy climb. The stairs are all different levels, but plenty of place to rest along the way, and the view at the top is so worth the effort.

reviews.author: Alex H
reviews.title: A great viewpoint of Tam Coc river
reviews.content: Parking with your scooter costed us 15,000. Make sure you just drive right up to the entrance and don’t use the shop vendors earlier on, no matter how much they wave at you and walk in front of your scooter.There are two viewpoints to see, one with the pagoda and one with the dragon overlooking the river. Can be done with moderate fitness and well worth the hike to the top.

reviews.author: Bill B
reviews.title: Do if in the area
reviews.content: Mua caves has a very nice entrance area leading up to the stairs.  Do ignore the people trying to flag you down as you get close to the attraction.  We simply said "No" and veered around them and they didn't bother us.  We were charged 10k each to park our bikes just outside the entrance to the attraction.  The stairs are steep and uneven so should be attempted by relatively fit people.  Gorgeous view from the top.  I recommend this attraction if you're in the area.

reviews.author: Polly
reviews.title: The lying dragon mountain
reviews.content: We cycled to the Mua Caves from our local accommodation, it is 5 vnd parking per bike. The entry fee is 100 vnd and soo worth it. When you enter the complex it is beautiful with little decorative ponds, views and swings and restaurants. It is a short walk to the start of the lying dragon mountain steps (view point). There are 500 steps, although wide, it is quite a steep ascend to the top and quite uneven. It is perfectly do able with good footwear and water and shouldn’t take too long if you have a good fitness level. The views are next level beautiful, really breathtaking. You have a view across the mountains but also down to the river where you can see the boats pass! A very rewarding climb! We would recommend getting there early to best the sun and the crowds for a more leisurely time.

reviews.author: DGSmanila
reviews.title: great view + sunset
reviews.content: for older guys - 500 stairs are not so easy as you might think :-)the climb is nice and the view from top is rewarding.We finished the day there so the sunset view is beautiful.

reviews.author: fal3
reviews.title: Great views at the top
reviews.content: We went in December so we couldn’t enjoy the green rice field’s however the view was still nice but rather brown. The steps are a bit slippery are poorly maintained. Weird given you pay a decent amount to get in. Overall I would consider this a must do in the Ninh Binh area along with the Trang An boat tour. It’s the only place here that gives a high vantage point.

reviews.author: Rickiray
reviews.title: Amazing views and worth it
reviews.content: The hike up isnt to tough, i would say moderate fitness you will be fine. We went for sunrise on a sunny day and were not disappointed, spectacular. WARNING about the parking area if you come by scooter or bicycle. Vendors will try to get you to park in their spots. There is parking inside the gate but it is limited   So the vendors outside do provide a needed service. Unfortunately they are way over aggresive and some not all that honest. They charge 15000 dong for a scooter “it is 10000 inside the gate”. A couple gave buddy 150000 dong by mistake and soon realized it he and pretended not to know what they were taking about. A big argument but it was pointless he didnt give back any change. We were parked in his stall and the scooter was still there when we got back so thats a plus. A shame as you could tell his parking spot is taken care of, it is the one on the right just as you reach the gate. They will jump right out in front of you and yell to get you into their stall. Be aware and try not to be intimidated.

reviews.author: Chris
reviews.title: Go for the top!
reviews.content: Every step on those 500 stairs we’ll get you closer to magnificent views! A very good exercise I’d do every day. Go early to avoid the tours coming from Hanoi. Also do the little Peak too, so you’ll have a better view of the tallest one.

reviews.author: MatthewTheCoder
reviews.title: Mua caves - day trip
reviews.content: We visited this site as part of the Ninh Binh day tours which cover Hoa Lu, Trang An and Mua caves.Mua caves has to be highlight of the 3 sites as part of the Ninh Binh day tour package. There are about 500 steps to the top. There are 2 climbs, one climb will lead you to a small feature token pagoda (not one where it can house people). The other climb is to the Dragon. The Dragon climb has a statue of Goddess of Mercy in front of the dragon's head.Some of the stairs are quiet steep. The overall climb can be a bit strenuous physically and that we were instructed by the tour guide to be back in the bus after 40 mins did not help.There were many tourists in this site. It is impossible when we were there to take a photo without someone being it it. There was also a queue on the way up the top of the Dragon peak.If you are short of time, the Dragon climb is better one, it is higher and has more challenging steps.The 40min given to us by the tour guide was simply not enough. I would spend perhaps 2 hours for this site alone, to adequately cover both peaks, catch your breath and enjoy the scenery. Pros: High recommended for the physical activity and the view at the top of the climb.  One of the many reasons to visit Ninh Binh.Cons: Too many tourists. There is literally a human traffic jam on the way up the 2 peaks.

reviews.author: Long H
reviews.title: Amazing view from Mua Cave
reviews.content: Mua Cave is so amazing, we had a great time to enjoy the panoramic view of Ninh BInh. 500 steps to reach the peak of mountain, definitely worth visiting. In the next visit, we will travel in the lotus season, cant' wait

reviews.author: Lorna M
reviews.title: A TIP I WAS GLAD TO KNOW!
reviews.content: Great view definitely worth the trip altough the locals as you the road that leads down to it run out pretending/demanding you park your bikes and pay. They blow whistles to look official and almost stand in your way not letting you by but make sure you just say no and keep driving past them until you get right upto the entrance. No matter how much they insist keep going. And then do not pay more than 5/10 thousand to park your bike (motorbike) bicycles should be less, either inside the gates at the official place which is 10 or you can haggle the guys at the entrance to 5/10. I seen some people paying 300/500! Or if you don't want to pay at all park before you turn onto the road somewhere and walk 5/10 minutes down the road and in.

reviews.author: Jocelyn C
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: Our group of seven aged 13-60+ visited Hang Mua. We all climbed to the peak. The views were worth the 400+ steps with great photo opportunities. The grounds and surrounds are lovely. It was quiet the morning we visited.

reviews.author: 630ph_ngl
reviews.title: Not like advertising
reviews.content: I guess it's nice to see the view once you reach the top, but when I was there it was incredibly busy, making the hike unpleasant. Also, the ride to this place is a complete tourist trap. When driving towards the ticket booth, locals will jump in front of your bike stating aggressively that you need to buy a parket ticket.. I'd advice people to keep on driving towards the ticket booth, as parking should be free there I believe, one more thing is not fair here is you have to pay for any time using toilet, not pleasant at all

reviews.author: hm777
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: Did not visit the caves, but visited Hang Mua peak, which provided beautiful views over the town landscape one side, and into a valley on the other side. The walk from the car park was full of interesting photo points, such as views over a lotus lake, swings, heart-shaped-vine structures, and statues you could sit on and pose with. There were lots of places to buy food and water and eat, and even water stops halfway up the mountain. To get to the mountain, you take the right fork at the path through the resort area. There are 2 peaks, and halfway up the mountain, you choose a path. Take the left fork to visit the tallest peak, with a dragon statue, or the right fork to visit a padoga on a narrow rocky outcrop. From the dragon peak, you can look over the pagoda peak, so if you don't have the energy for both, I'd recommend taking the left fork for the dragon. Note that there will likely be people climbing all over the rocks around the dragon statue!

reviews.author: Gabi C
reviews.title: Not a cave but excellent lookout point
reviews.content: You have to climb up steps to get to a couple of different lookout platforms, views are stunning! You can look over Ninh Binh or over the Tam Coc river ride and rice paddies. There are also lotus flower fields that you can take pictures in. Mua Caves is accessed through the Eco Resort so there are restaurants and places to buy drinks and ice-cream (which you will need after the climb!)Very beautiful and worth it!

reviews.author: John C
reviews.title: Double check direction, don’t just go by Google maps
reviews.content: Beautiful scenery and well worth the climb, our only downfall was we wanted to be up for sunset and left our hostel at 5 for a 15 min drive but Google maps left us down big time brought us to too many dead ends and pointless routes, we would have been lost without google maps throughout our 3 months trip, but for this one journey it is best to ask reception how to get there.

reviews.author: Julian Klassen
reviews.title: Just great
reviews.content: It was great and I will never forget. Nice place outside of crowded cities.  Definitely come back one day. Worth to climb up to the mountain

reviews.author: Raahul Prashanth
reviews.title: Day hike
reviews.content: Mua caves hike was really tiresome if you want to climb both the peaks. I climbed during the sunset and it had an amazing view.It's worth the sweat to climb this viewpoint.

reviews.author: camuche123
reviews.title: What a climb !
reviews.content: Not so many people so perfect to climb. It was very hot so take some water and u can buy some at mid way in case. View from the top is impressive on both side. Great for photos and memories of deep Vietnam

reviews.author: Travelandfood
reviews.title: A great place to visit
reviews.content: If you are visiting Ninh Binh, This is a must see. We were traveling from Hanoi to Hoi An on our motorbike and we stopped here for a night. The walk is not for everyone, but you will be glad you visited this place. Enjoy

reviews.author: Vietnam Escape Tour Travel
reviews.title: Really nice place but not for elderly
reviews.content: That is really good place for a view to Tam Coc. However, you should not do it too late at noon because it is a tired and not really good when it is sunny and when you are hungry. it is not for elderly also.The best time to go there from March to end of may.i did it in April when it was not too hot but i could see the rice field.Really recommend this place for young travellers.If you have time please stay overnight in Tam Coc or Trang An then do a morning cycling to Mua Cave in the early morning for hiking when you still have a lot of anergy.

reviews.author: ernur
reviews.title: Because it is Ninh Binh Province
reviews.content: İt is easy to reach from Hanoi. You may try daily tours or overnight at this place. Our choice was second one and spend 2 days. Mua caves is the top place of Ninh Binh. You may see all mountains, rivers and boats easily. The weather forecast is not good for this area. Because of micro-climate, you may face with sunny weather even if there is thunderstorm at forecast.  500 steps up and it is worth to see the beatuy of whole area. September is also good choice for visiting. Stable weather, green rice paddies, less humidity. Stop thinking and just let go this place.

reviews.author: Tracy Duong
reviews.title: Best to visit in the harvest season
reviews.content: I love the way riding around Trang An area. The view from Hang Mua is also good. Better to come here on sunny days and in the harvest season and enjoy stunning golden paddy fields,

reviews.author: Karolina S
reviews.title: AMAZING!!
reviews.content: Fantastic day out! The place really exceeded my expectations. It's a lot of stops (around 500?) to climb up, and in Vietnamese heat it can be quite challenging but the views up top are REALLY worth it :) there's a lot to do and see and the whole place makes for a great half day out.

reviews.author: Victoria Teresa
reviews.title: Long climb
reviews.content: Long climb to the top but has good views. Not a lot of support in terms of safety and rocks can be slippery at times so it's worthwhile to be careful here. The view is good but due to the air quality and smog you can't really see too far. It was interesting to see the country side and how locals live on the drive there.

reviews.author: amanda5805
reviews.title: Quiet & picturesque place to spend a half day!
reviews.content: We arrived at the Mua Caves around 11:30am. There is a ton to see here and the hour and a half we got here was not even close to enough time. Not a ton of people which was nice. It cost 100,000VND (about $6CAD).We started with a quick tiger cave tour. There is an underground stream deep inside cave other than that there is not much to it. If you are here a short time skip the cave. Then we were off  to climb the 486 stone steps to the top of the mountains to see the incredible views over the rice fields and Tam Coc river. It is a long, hot climb but worth it when you see the incredible views. The stairs and hand rails are very well maintained. There is also a few spots that you can pull off to the side to have a quick rest. It took us about 35mins to get to the top with a few quick rest stops. I am also very out of shape. Some people can do it in 20-25mins. It is very steep but very wide. There is 2 peaks you can go to. We only had enough time to do one. So we picked the the dragon peak side. Instead if the Pagoda Side. There is some fun swings, places to have a snack, walkway over the rice fields and so much more. It is a great place to slow life down and enjoy the beauty and the quiet. Our guide said you can actually stay just outside the site. If we are ever back I will be looking into that. We were running low on time so we did a quick walk threw the rice fields. There are washrooms but you must pay 2000VND (.12 cents CAD) a person.  Make sure you have small bills how they did not give change. There was no toilet paper so pack some with you same with hand sanitizer.

reviews.author: Magdalene Nettles
reviews.title: 500 steps to a magnificent view
reviews.content: We did this on a trip. The measures are very high plus we showed up right before lunchtime and this was really quite a night before we had a great deal of rainfall so measures have been a little slippery on the way that down. When at the best you've wrestling with the crowds to obtain a picture together with the dragon. Not a great deal of space for lots of individuals being there right away. The point of view is amazing and worth the climb. You are able to understand why they call it Halong bay on land. There's a few of nice tourist shops just where we could have the ability to look and never be harassed. It will were good to get enough time to ascend another peak to own a great photo shoot of the key climb.

reviews.author: Jean D
reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.content: The views from the top are absolutely breathtaking, so the climbing those infamous 500 steps is definitely worth it!

reviews.author: nina
reviews.title: Pleasant area, but need to get up a lot of stairs
reviews.content: Better go here from Nov to Feb, as it's cooler. When u go in the summertime, it is going to be very hot and also you do not possess the power to get up all of the stairways that around thousand steps. It is not uncomplicated to get up and so take care. Take the time of yours and enjoy the view

reviews.author: micheal
reviews.title: Nice spot but crowded
reviews.content: Coming from Ha Giang Loop and after getting Ma Pi Ling Pass, it is typically hard to see anything better.This specific place is just 1 hour from Hanoi, with access which is simple, therefore a large amount of individuals go to open it.A good workout to climb the stairs, although you are rewarded with great views. Unfortunately, the silence this particular place needs is corrupted but the people.I did not strive for the cave as I am not a great appreciator of them.Do not overlook on the counter a passage, like a cave, which provides us permission to use the places on the other side

reviews.author: Eridere
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Is it a bit touristy? YepIs it worth going? YepIs it underrated? YepSo glad we ignored the naysayers and drove here from Hanoi. The scenery was spectacular, the climbs were fine, easy pictures to take, and the boat ride was fantastic. Whether you are at the top looking down or on the river looking up....this is a great spot. It's basically Halong Bay on solid earth with a river flowing under the mountains.Don't miss it.

reviews.author: Marlon
reviews.title: Panoramic views of a lovely landscape
reviews.content: The 500 step climb was simpler than I anticipated, possibly due to the cool weather. For all those that are reluctant to get up, trust me it is going to be worthwhile. The perspective from the best seems as a scene from a film.

reviews.author: Sargent Mercer
reviews.title: The most effective experience
reviews.content: The point of view is exceptional. You must take shoes that are great cause the actions are extremely high. The ideal spot to invest the sunset. I would not advocate climbing up the steps aged individuals or maybe women that are expectant.

reviews.author: Ortiz
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: This particular place is Halong Bay on farm land, with a lot of less places. Remain at Tam Coc Garden hotel and do a bicycle ride if at all possible. It's safe to drive there as well as beautiful. The cave is simply a title, the answer is hiking the hill for a fantastic perspective.

reviews.author: Barnabas
reviews.title: Gorgeous views but look out for intense locals
reviews.content: The Mua Cave viewpoint provides breathtaking views of the Vietnamese countryside. Its an intense hike on the top so ensure that you not pick the hottest day of the week. One time in the pinnacle, there's a bit of hut that provides a little shade and also you are able to get all over the dragon statue for many great photos. Since the pinnacle is very tiny it is able to get hectic.While the view is extremely recommendable, getting there wasn't an extremely enjoyable experience. We arrived for a motorbike and the moment we hit the highway the leads to the cave there was locals vigorously attempting to help make us park at the spots of theirs. We werent conscious of this beforehand so we made the error of stopping at 1 of those locations. After signaling  we wished to start working on the conclusion of the highway, the person started to shout at us in Vietnamese and also whistled at or even faces until we eventually was able to go around her. Other locals jumped before our scooted and attempted to prevent it by pushing against it from the front side. The most effective method of getting through this street is most likely to help keep on going and shaking the head/beeping of yours at virtually any regional who attempts to stop you.

reviews.author: Cymbre
reviews.title: Worth the effort
reviews.content: Did this included in a motorbike tour with Tommy's tours. It was incredible and in case you are able to perform the 500 actions worth the hassle as the sights plus image possibilities are limitless.

reviews.author: Brett Ilyunin
reviews.title: Great view from the top part, terrible caves
reviews.content: The point that you've paying as well as cover parking lost the a star.The caves are not well worth the journey, though the climb is! There's a lovely view from the best in case you do not sweat to death before you can get there.Go early on to stay away from visitors as well as the heat

reviews.author: Tatiania
reviews.title: Hot but good views
reviews.content: Views are impressive bug it's actually a climb in the high temperature. Watch for the parking scams with extremely intense parking attendants.

reviews.author: Twelve S
reviews.title: Beautiful and Fun Experience
reviews.content: Our tour guide arranged for us to take this famous boat ride through the caves in Ninh Binh. It's just about the quietest 90 minutes we experienced while traveling with our kids. Our guide advised us to tip the rower with cash instead of snacks, as you will be pressured to do. We did this AFTER hiking to the top of the Flying Dragon and I'm glad because it was fun to look up at where we had been.

reviews.author: RG02
reviews.title: Not really a ‘cave’
reviews.content: There is a small cave but it’s the long stairway to get the views from the top of the mountain that make this place worth visiting. Most visitors want to do the climb to the top, which is worth the entrance fee, but if you have a partner who is unable to cope with the very uneven stairway there is no option to enter the garden area without paying the full price, they would probably spend at least that amount in one of the shops or cafes inside. The views from the top are spectacular in every direction and it’s worth making the effort if you are able to.

reviews.author: Kathrine S
reviews.title: Worth the walk
reviews.content: In the beginning, the 500 uneven steps does appear a tad daunting. But there's a lot of little areas to rest. See the breath of yours back. Have a picture and go on the climb on the top.Items are just a little out of hand in the dragon. Nevertheless, there's ample room for a picture.

reviews.author: Timi B
reviews.title: A most scenic hike
reviews.content: I was not certain in case I needed to perform the 700 odd things but made it happen in the long run. Well well worth the climb. Perspective in the pinnacle was really spectacular

reviews.author: Pavlov C
reviews.title: The view is nice but doesn't be duped by phony parking!
reviews.content: Don't be duped by the fake "parking" across the little road to the Mua Cave. They behave really aggressively to help you get to the parking of theirs, acting as officials with effective hand gestures and whistles. Simply ignore next and also go on traveling until the ticket office of Mua entrance. Generally there you are able to park the motorcycle of yours for VND 10,000. Entrance to Mua is VND 100,000 a person.The climb was hot and steep, but much worthwhile as the view from the pinnacle is stunning!

reviews.author: Canas
reviews.title: A little physical but absolutely worthwhile!
reviews.content: Incredible landscapes after you turn up in the pinnacle. Quite possibly on the manner in which, every little thing is beautiful. Quite a great deal of stairs to get though it is worth every penny!

reviews.author: Emberton
reviews.title: The mountain of its
reviews.content: We believed that its the incorrect name when said " Mua cave".Because the key thing because of this place is hiking to the best mountain to find out the area view. The cave is simply little.

reviews.author: Klimontovich
reviews.title: Several of the most incredible views in Vietnam
reviews.content: A really very popular hike up 2 large peaks, to discover completely stunning views across the mountains. In hindsight, we want we'd shot the boat from Tam Coc to the caves and back however we just had one day so we did not have an opportunity to accomplish this.

reviews.author: litrella2
reviews.title: A lovely tourist destination and also must visit Ninh Binh
reviews.content: The view from above on the rice fields and rocky method and the river of Ninh Binh. The point of view is wonderful and beautiful very. Climb up two peaks aproximatelly 200m to find a panoramic view of Tam Coc. Don't miss this attraction.Weekends are crowded with numerous people

reviews.author: Porrett
reviews.title: Bird's eye view of Tam Coc
reviews.content: It will take 500 steps to attain the best, but believe in me its worth every penny! It might be a little challenging to attain the best with kids. Stay away from the climb throughout the noontime and attempt to achieve there simply after four when the sunshine is not really too warm. Mua cave is situated alongside a resort so there are lots of restaurants and stores available close by. Carry a container of water along with you!

reviews.author: Plampin
reviews.title: Impressive view
reviews.content: It is extremely tough to get as much as the pinnacle in an extremely popular Day. I simply are able to do some point though the view & environment from the pinnacle was superb. A must do!

reviews.author: Griffin Dibb
reviews.title: Trek to Mua caves viewpoints
reviews.content: Better to go early morning also it is possible in case you reside in the Mua Caves Ecolodge. You will find two components, to the correct results in a pagoda view as well as the stairway to the left on the dragon viewpoint showcasing the meandering river with the limestone rock formations laced with correct fields alongside. A lot of people are able to go over the climb unless there's a pre existing medical problem preventing it. We noticed individuals that are older  with walking sticks similarly performing the climb. It normally takes 45mins to two hours based on the rate and also level of fitness.

reviews.author: dandynette
reviews.title: viewpoint is amazing
reviews.content: The cave is unrelevant, but the view is incredible. Going to the viewpoint is not so far, but it's exausting. After you can enjoy the complex, bar, restaurant, swimming pool, parc for children. it's lovely area.quite expensive 100 000 vd

reviews.author: Wilbert B
reviews.title: Very best views of Vietnam.
reviews.content: Experience that is amazing to find out the ideas from the best and touch the dragon for a benefit. So far as parking be kind to the locals and lease the areas and are just attempting to make a buck to live. Be polite and simply keep on traveling within the gate. I'd absolutely no difficulties. The parking issue you are going to find in the slightest venues and so just constantly visit the venue and its a sure bet.

reviews.author: Gifford Bovingdon
reviews.title: Incredible View from the Top
reviews.content: We cycled right here from Tam Coc early on one morning, arriving aproximatelly 6.45 am. It was quiet and a good moment being out and also about. It absolutely was a trek to the pinnacle of the hill and I hardly believe I've previously sweated very much though it had been worthwhile for the fantastic, panoramic views. Stunning. The park or perhaps whatever it's in the feet of the hill is quite strange though we walked straight through which. We didnt look at the caves. The single criticism of mine is about the rubbish all up the steps and on top. An entry fee is charged so please use several of it to deal with the ugly rubbish! Dont spoil this gorgeous site by disregarding the rubbish! And get the rubbish of yours away along with you if you see, dont simply toss it on the ground. The thing about Vietnam which I simply dont comprehend at all.

reviews.author: Adrian F
reviews.title: A must-do experience if you are physically able
reviews.content: If you are able to walk up a few hundred steep steps you will be treated to some incredible views of this region from Mua Cave Viewpoint. We visited in the afternoon when it was quite busy and so would recommend visiting early morning if you wish to avoid a lot of people. But it is well worth the effort and you will get some amazing photographs of the mountainous scenery.

reviews.author: Explorer
reviews.title: Majestic view..worth the climb
reviews.content: Be prepared to climb the stairs. About 502 stairs. but its worth it. the view from top is amazing. but the last climb to the dragon is dangerous. not recommended for kids and old ppl. as long as you reach the peak, its good.

reviews.author: G2Kpauly
reviews.title: Fantastic!
reviews.content: I really enjoyed the view from the top! Well worth the walk. Could have easily spent 3 hours if we had got there earlier. Many paths you can walk around. No sunset unfortunately though as cloudy.

reviews.author: Dee_LW_36
reviews.title: Surpassed expectations
reviews.content: Incredible views over the beautiful landscape in this area. If arriving by motorbike or bike you can park right by the ticket booth (instead of believing the guy at the top who told us we needed to pay their and walk down 😉)

reviews.author: Shachar C
reviews.title: Fantastic views
reviews.content: I wouldn't bother with the caves or the touristic area below. The climb up the mountain is worth every bit of effort as the views are truely unique.

reviews.author: silvergeck0
reviews.title: Very neglected and disappointing
reviews.content: Getting to the top was a personal achievement and while that was incredible and the views amazing the area surrounding the climb at Hung  Mua was very disappointing.  It’s advertised as an Eco/Environmental location; however there is rubbish EVERYWHERE (something that has surprised & disappointed us about Vietnam in general). In this tourist hot spot there is Rubbish piled up under trees and beside the little display houses.  The toilets were absolutely disgusting with water from the basin leaking over the floor. The shops at the bottom of the stairs were in complete disarray and dirty too.  We saw the pool getting cleaned and the water was being back washed into the lagoon! Surely the chlorine will kill the fish and plants? We were there on a quiet day and there must have been at least 2000 people during the few hours we were there - it’s 100,000 VD entrance fee so in our opinion there is no excuse for the owners to allow what should be magnificent to become so ugly.

reviews.author: Beth
reviews.title: Insta worthy picture opportunities
reviews.content: Initially you walk through a little eco resort where there are Instagram scenes set up, like a wooden heart structure and other such things. The caves themselves are a bit meh. We visited for no more than 5 minutes. The main attraction is the two karsts to climb. Not the easiest of ascents with uneven and slippery steps but they're worth the views!

reviews.author: Lily P
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: Nice view from the top . It is difficult for the elderly, the ladder is not safe especially on rainy days. If you ride a motorbike, you should ask for the parking fee first. I was subjective and didn't ask them then they charged us 25,000 Vietnamese dong for one (the price of other stores is only 300 meters away only 5,000VND for one)

reviews.author: Victoria
reviews.title: Not really worth it
reviews.content: We went to mua cave because it was said the view is amazing... The view is ok but we had beter. They turned the place to a sort of tourist park, that lost it autenticity.

reviews.author: Zarela
reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.content: Great place to climbing up the mountain, from the peak of the mountain you can enjoy the amazing view with rice fields and rivers.

reviews.author: Erik Hoang, Nguyen
reviews.title: Great view from above !!!
reviews.content: It's perfect to climbing. Almost clean but still have rubbish. So crowd and if you want to take a nice picture, please be patient to wait. And remember to wear a brogues.

reviews.author: coco928
reviews.title: Don’t overthink the stairs
reviews.content: Don’t be scared of the stairs. Everyone was talking about how many stairs there were to the top where the dragon is. the stairs were no big deal. Take it slow, enjoy the views and GO see the top! It’s well worth the walk up the stairs. The only negative is pushy tourists at the top and people holding on to the dragon is starting to break it. Some reviews discussed the high entry fee. Really? It’s the equivalent of around $4. Cheap for the views, walks and scenic area.

reviews.author: Morten Bay Madsen
reviews.title: Beautiful view and a small exercise to spice it up.!
reviews.content: Wonderful view on top after a fairly easy walk to the top. Some steps are more accesible than others.BEWARE of the people trying to persuade You to park Your bike/scooter along the dirt road to the entrance. Drive all the way to the ticket office and park there.

reviews.author: Alan
reviews.title: Pretty good hike and view
reviews.content: We motorbiked here and google maps took us to the wrong place at first, so check maps ahead of time to make sure it is correct. The hike itself was pretty good, and when you get to the top theres a great view. On the bottom, theres a resort of some kind, with a pool and some scenic places to take photos.

reviews.author: Natascha
reviews.title: Nice View!
reviews.content: First we were a bit shocked about the price 100’000 Dong (4 Dollar) just for walking up some stairs. But it was absolutely worth it! Amazing View and workout done for the day (500 Steps)!

reviews.author: JSTrip_77
reviews.title: Absolutely Incredibly But You Must Be FIT!!
reviews.content: Ironically, this site is called Mua Caves. But, the principal attraction is the massive stone staircases to two separate overlooks. But BOTH overlooks require climbing up 500+ uneven stone steps. It's really not for those who are afraid of heights or are not physically fit. If you go on a tour, you don't have to worry about any of this but if you go on your own, you'll find that as you drive toward the site, you'll start seeing tons of opportunities to pay for parking. Eventually, you will have to stop and pay. But, I'd recommend continuing to drive as far as you can toward the site before stopping. We were initially charged 50,000 for parking but I negotiated to 30,000 as 50,000 would have been the most expensive parking I'd encountered in Vietnam. Then, you pay per person (100,000 dong - also expensive compared to other sites) and continue on. Eventually, you'll get to a  sign that tells you to go left to the cave and right to the overlooks. Everyone including us went right. We figured that we'd do the cave if we had time. In the end, we did have time to do the cave too. Have done the Trang An caves the day before, this wasn't the most impressive of caves but it was still cool. But, don't go for the cave, go for the overlooks!

reviews.author: Sarah Luong
reviews.title: Spectacular scenery
reviews.content: Mua Cave is one of the most attractive destinations in Ninh Binh area. After climbing about 500 steps, you will see a very spectacular scenery, overlooking the rocky mountains, rivers, fields, bamboo boats.I had planned to go to Ninh Binh with my boyfriend 2 days 1 night. The best advice to visit the Mua Cave is to get there early (I started climbing at 6:30 am). The sunrise at the top was very beautiful, and there were not too many people, so I felt completely relaxed. Many people say that the sunset is even more beautiful, but in the afternoon there are many tourists so you will find it difficult to take photos and enjoy the natural beauty. I have taken some nice photos to post on Instagram and I enjoyed the fresh air with the boyfriend while looking at the scenery there, so I feel that this destination is worth a visit if you come to Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: XavierNY
reviews.title: Fun and Nice View
reviews.content: Come here for that amazing view of the rice fields and Ninh Bin. If taking a motobike like me, please ignore the people going out in the street to try to make you park, they will harass the hell out of you but just go straight and you can park in the Mua Cave entrance for free. The view is nice but I want in January and the rice fields were mostly brown, still enjoyed it and worth the journey. I did this in a day trip from Hanoi and did Tam Coc as well with a lunch inbetween, it was a fun day! (Took 8:50am train from Hanoi and returned on a 6:45 train from Ninh Bin, rented motorbike outside the train station for 100VND) Enjoy.

reviews.author: Der-Chillian
reviews.title: Nice View but gets crowded easily.
reviews.content: After reading the other reviews we decided to go there quite early in the morning. You can pass by all (!) the guys and lady’s that try to lure your into their (overpriced!) parking and put your bike inside the walled area of the hotel at the end of the road. Tickets were 100k each, and the climb is quite exhausting. But the view rewards you and is completely worth it. As we walked down it really started to get busy and we were quite happy to have been there at 8:15pm. We did not visit the caves. Sadly there is quite some trash on the stairs and on top of the mountain.

reviews.author: Emilie G
reviews.title: Beautiful viewpoint
reviews.content: Beautiful viewpoint. We would recommend it at sunset as it is particularly beautiful. It is a busy site. Also, not indicating 5/5 as we had to face aggressive locals on the way who wanted to force us to pay a higher price for parking our bicycles. And then, when we stopped at the official one, one of the guys working there also tried to trick us. Go and ask the price at the ticket office. This first experience ruins a bit the whole visit.

reviews.author: lovisaduvander
reviews.title: Breathtaking view
reviews.content: Beautiful place, not as hard as people said it would be! It’s a lot of stairs of course but I’m not a very athletic person and it took me about 25 minutes to get to the top of the dragon! You can stop along the way and see the beautiful view but worth going all the way up cause it was beautiful! One thing I didn’t like was the actual Park was very touristy! A lot of people and it’s a lot of fake flowers etc, which is beautiful don’t get me wrong. But just not what I need on a trip in Vietnam ;) Usually on the top it’s a queue to get to the dragon but worth going up. It’s very very hard to stand up there and you need to be careful, you literally need to climb so know that this is not a security or anything like that so just be careful if you go to the top!

reviews.author: Hien Huynh
reviews.title: Nice place, but have to climb up so many stairs
reviews.content: Bettee go here during Nov to Feb, as it is cooler. If u go in summer time, it will be super hot and u dont have the energy to climb up all the stair which around 1000 step. Its not easy to climb up so becareful. Take ur time and enjoy the view

reviews.author: Cameron Y
reviews.title: A must see in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: The demanding climb will reward you with amazing views.  Take your time negotiating your way to the dragon at the top. The rocks are sharp but the riskier task is negotiating your way around tourists in the tight space.Tip. If you are riding a motorbike, avoid the parks and "parking attendants" further from the start.  Take your bike up to the starting point for the walk.  You will see bike parks on the left. I paid VND10000(USD50c approx)

reviews.author: theresabryson65
reviews.title: Long climb
reviews.content: This is a long climb and visitors need to be aware it is steep in places. I have arthritis in my hips but managed it slowly. Some of the lower facilities were a little scruffy but in all an excellent experience.

reviews.author: digitalroc
reviews.title: Amazing view of Tam Coc
reviews.content: Worth the time and effort to get here, as you are awarded with a spectacular view of Tam Coc!  The added 10 foot climb to stand near the Dragon is just check mark that you did it, as there isn’t much room at the atop the jagged rock.  Ensure you wear proper foot wear, as you will need it!

reviews.author: Mushtaq N
reviews.title: I HOPE THIS HELPS YOU ALL
reviews.content: First of all i gave it 3 stars just for the views otherwise it is not worth the 100,000VD entrance fee and 10,000VD parking fee, use that money for Tran An. After reading the reviews i prepared myself for the aggressive locals, to avoid them make sure you go early in the morning ideally before 9am. We only encountered 2 of them and when they tried to stop my bike i just went past them. Ignore their whistles and head straight to the entrance. We got to both the view points with only a few other people so we had the whole place to ourselves because most of the tourist coaches arrive after 10am. When we left the place we saw that there were around 8 locals now trying to stop people.

reviews.author: Barney T
reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.content: It’s a great climb up to the view point, and one of the most beautiful place in Tam Cox area. Only thing why not 5* it’s because of some local people who are rudely pushing you to park your scooter in their place, and asking for 10k+ for it...

reviews.author: Alan S
reviews.title: Worth the walk
reviews.content: At first the 400+ uneven steps does seem a bit daunting. But there is plenty of small areas to rest. Get your breath back. Take a photo and continue the climb to the top.Things are a little out of control at the dragon. However there is enough space for a photo.Suggest to go before it gets too hot.

reviews.author: NtshuaL
reviews.title: Amazing views, worth the hike!
reviews.content: Beautiful hike up. It was humid, but anyone can make it! Bring plenty of water! We biked to the entrance and parked our bikes in after the gate (it's free). There will be a lot of people trying to tell you to pay to park at their lot but don't do it. Just keep going in until you get past the entrance gate where you pay for admission. We went a few hours before sunset and was able to complete it and back before it got too dark. At the top there is a big white dragon statue, which is supposedly the watcher of the town. Definitely worth the steps!

reviews.author: Anna M
reviews.title: Great view but so crowded!
reviews.content: There were so many people it really made the whole visit difficult.  As we walked up & down the stairs we constantly needed to avoid people posing for photos.   Once we got to the top it was much worse with people practically crawling over one another to get to the best photo spot. Also terrifying to watch some people clamber to the very edge in search of the perfect photo.  Lovely view when we managed to get to the front of the crowd though.  We visited on 1 January (public holiday) late afternoon so not sure if it might be less crowded at other times.

reviews.author: Teresa
reviews.title: good walk
reviews.content: was a nice walk up to the dragon a bit steep in places but well worth the views from the top worthwile

reviews.author: Richard Kay
reviews.title: Tourist trap, too many tourists to enjoy the view.
reviews.content: Quite simply we felt very underwhelmed by our trip. A decent view but far too many people climbing at once to enjoy it. Too many taking up space for Instagram photos. The area at the bottom of the caves is full of fake nonsense, fake waterfalls, fake statues etc: Save your money and time, go to the boat ride at Trang An which is absolutely stunning and far more relaxing!

reviews.author: sandra s
reviews.title: Tough climb up but did it
reviews.content: We wanted to go up to the dragon mountain so we climbed for like 30mins where then you decide to Turn Right or left. Left to the dragon and right to the pagoda. Pagoda has steps all the way up but it is still lower than the dragon mountain. For the dragon mountain, it’s another 15mins to the TOP. But you can’t see the dragon. You have to scale some rocks and jump across and down somewhere to reach the dragon head. Beyond that, it was even more dangerous so we stopped at the head only. Also very narrow and have to wait for people to go up or down before your turn. And remember it’s not a path, but just rocks. Not for the older folks at this point. It’s really beautiful anywhere you stop cos it’s really high already, you can see all the other mountain tops and also down below the delta. Breathtaking.

reviews.author: Rajalakshmy M
reviews.title: Nice climb and an excellent view
reviews.content: We took a bike from our resort to the caves. There is an eco lodge at the base and a lotus pond. Well maintained. We went on a day with little fog . But it was very enjoyable and worth the climb. You get a great view of Tam Coc from up there.

reviews.author: Charlotte P
reviews.title: Incredible views! A must-do in tamcoc or ninh binh
reviews.content: Located approximately 5km away from tamcoc, Mua caves was a short bicycle ride from my home stay. Once you’ve parked up your bike and paid the entrance fee (100,000 VND) you can roam around the lake and lily fields or climb to 500 stairs to the top. Two-thirds of the way up the path divides into two peaks, giving you panoramic views of the area. Bring water with you as there’s limited shade during the middle of the day.

reviews.author: Rob B
reviews.title: A must-do if you’re in the area
reviews.content: There are a few stairs to climb but not to bad. The views are well worth the effort. We had a pretty hazy day but still enjoyed the views.The very top ( along the dragon ) can be dangerous if you’re not very careful. So just take it slow and find a place to sit and just soak it all in.

reviews.author: GavinPortland
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: This location is Halong Bay on land, with lots fewer places.  Stay at Tam Coc Garden hotel and do a bike ride if possible.  It is safe to ride there and gorgeous.  The cave is just a name, the key is to hike the hill for a great view.

reviews.author: Neisha Sen
reviews.title: Trek to Mua caves view points
reviews.content: Best to go early morning and its convenient if you live within the Mua Caves Ecolodge. There are 2 parts, to the right leads to a pagoda viewpoint and the stairway to the left to the dragon view point showcasing the meandering river through the limestone rock formations laced with right fields alongside. Most people can navigate the climb unless there is a pre-existing medical condition preventing it. We saw old people with walking sticks also doing the  climb. It takes 45mins to 2 hours depending on the pace and fitness level.

reviews.author: Durga M
reviews.title: Excellent voew
reviews.content: There is a Dragon at the top of the mountain and the view from the top was breathtaking.There are almost 1000 stairs both sides and please be prepared to take raincoats as our travel agent forgot and we were completely drenched But the experience was awesome

reviews.author: Rico
reviews.title: Climb to the Dragon!
reviews.content: This is definitely one of the coolest attractions in the area! You need to have some level of conditioning to handle the steps and to climb around the razor sharp rock at the top by the Dragon. The views looking in all directions are awesome. You can’t get enough photos. Even if you can’t climb the stairs there is enough reason to visit. At the bottom they had an excellent lotus field with a wooden walkway. There were rice fields beyond that and picture perfect karst small mountains beyond that! I mean, WOW! Also, there is a little village eating area complete with waterfall and a beautifully done pond, sculptures, bonsai trees, ponds with steppingstones everything was well decorated there were balloons and small bridges with walkways. Truly well built and there was plenty to eat and drink too. Not to mention the caves which are easy too access. You need a good amount of time to see and explore it all. We recommend you bring plenty of water for the climb up the steps. We chose to go in the afternoon when the steps were in the shade and the sunlight was great for getting pictures over the rice and lotus fields. This place is a must visit when in Ninh Binh.We highly recommend it!

reviews.author: Ruth C
reviews.title: Steps steps & more steps!
reviews.content: Cycled to Mua cave and lying dragon mountain from our homestay. Despite it being a cloudy day we had pretty good views when we climbed up. Many locals were trying to get us to park our bicycles with them and they seemed a bit more insistent with motorcycle riders. We parked at the ticket counter for 10,000 each. Entrance fee is 100,000. The steps up the mountain weren't as bad as I thought and there are many spots to stop and take a break and some beautiful photos. It was a bit difficult climbing around the dragon statue as it's a bit of a one way system and everyone is trying to get up and down at the same time. The mua cave itself opens up to a peaceful forested area but the cave itself isn't much. All in all it's worth the trip out for the views!!!

reviews.author: zaawaaz
reviews.title: Try to visit on weekday
reviews.content: Clean place, primed for tourists. Some shops inside. The caves were underwhelming. The views at the top 2 peaks were OK, but too many people taking photos everywhere on a weekend. 😅 Helpful locals helped me on my way to the end of the dragon. Really lovely people. Steps are OK, just wear good soles. Go during summer - May or Apr? 👍🏻 Aerial view is not the best in vietnam but still nice to see Tam Coc in better seasons. Stay in one of the hotels nearby would be good for sunrise sunset.

reviews.author: Lara A
reviews.title: High up above
reviews.content: Lovely place and fabulous View! Go and see the sunset. Prepare to climb high up above. Good for exercising!

reviews.author: Bo B
reviews.title: No 500 steps
reviews.content: After only 200 steps I found it not possible, despite good condition, for a man aged 75 to climb the 500 steps. Disappointing to sit waiting for the others in the bus tour.

reviews.author: Kelsey S
reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.content: This was a great stop! The views are stunning especially at sunset. The hike was easy for me as I’m in good shape, but I went with my 60-70 year old parents and we took it slow. They were very nervous as they’re not in the best shape, but they survived and said it was worth it. The only downside is my mom is very short and some steps are very tall, so it was hard for her short legs. But all in all it’s totally worth it even if you’re in bad shape. For perspective, even going super slow and stopping for pictures, we made it to the top within 20-30 minutes.

reviews.author: lpollard80
reviews.title: Very beautiful! Nice day if you want to escape the city.
reviews.content: Visiting this area was one of my favorite days in Vietnam. We took a boat ride, hiked and biked. The sunset was incredible. Go check it out, you won't be disappointed.

reviews.author: F.C./SUI
reviews.title: Full of trash.....
reviews.content: We rented a scooter and we drove very early to this place. Arrival at 5.30 a.m. - 100k entrance fee & 15k parking fee - about 500 steps up to the top and there we enjoyed the wonderful sunrise ;-)It's a beautiful place with amazing cliffs, beautiful view, everything fine so far... BUT.... we just give 3 stars because of the plastic & trash. So sad to see that everywhere was trash. At the ground, between the cliffs, everywhere! We pay 100k per person but they just earn monney and do nothing!! Sad to see...

reviews.author: Caroline V
reviews.title: spectacular views
reviews.content: If you are planning to skip this, reconsider! We were doubting as it's very touristic, but the views are really worth it!

reviews.author: TCav
reviews.title: Stunning views! A must climb!
reviews.content: I completed this in Dec 19, climbing the steps to the incredible viewpoint at the top! A 120,000D entrance fee to the attraction, with 15,000D parking fee for bike or scooter, means its a little more expensive than the regular site in the area, but worth every penny. As soon as you enter the site, you are hit with stunning waterfalls and bridges for photo opportunities before the big climb. At the top, the city view and mountain sites are breathtaking. Even in the dark, you can see the outlines of the mountains in the distance and see the achievement of how far you’ve climbed. A definite do for sunset!

reviews.author: MidnightFrog
reviews.title: Great view, super crowded
reviews.content: We came late in the day with a small tour group. Honestly, we weren't expecting much given the large number of tourists but once at the top of was pretty nice. Several wedding parties taking pictures added to the crowded charm and the late day sun and clouds made for a great scene over the valley.

reviews.author: Mathieu R
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: Very touristic attraction, you go up a hill with A LOT of tourists taking selfies all around. The view is quite nice, but is it worth it? It all depends on your tolerence towards very touristic attractions. Personally, I think this is very skippable.

reviews.author: Bene M
reviews.title: Amazing place
reviews.content: You can come here to visite the caves, go on 2 mountains to have an great view and enjoy sundown, visit the lotusflower-field or enjoy pool or some games for children! I like this places even there are so many tourists

reviews.author: NaimahCallachand
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: Absolutely beautiful views from the top of the Mua caves. Entrance fee is 100000 VD, and it’s about 500 steps to the top which are quite steep so would recommend wearing good footwear. Views are absolutely fantastic ! Worth going to both peaks!

reviews.author: SunnyNg249
reviews.title: Gorgeous view from the top
reviews.content: Visit here in March at about 11am. Thanks God it was cool and windy so it wasn’t really hard climb. After around 550 steps, the view was absolutely amazing. It was quite busy on top which made it hard to get a good photo. Highly recommend you bring some water for hiking.

reviews.author: Jac Teo
reviews.title: A most scenic hike
reviews.content: Wasn't sure if I wanted to do the 700 odd steps but did it in the end. Well worth the climb. View at the top was absolutely spectacular

reviews.author: Stephen G
reviews.title: Amazing view!
reviews.content: Love the view from the top of dancing cave mountain. After hiking up for 15minutes, you will see the Tam Coc river from the high peak. It worth the exercising!

reviews.author: Dario Bento
reviews.title: Wonderful views
reviews.content: You can visit the garden and watch the locals fishing. There’s also some rice fields around.The best part comes after climbing almost 600 steps. You’ll have an amazing view from the top. It’s worthed!

reviews.author: Mawebb
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: I rode a bike from Tam Coc, The ride was enjoyable, at the end ignore everyone wanting you to park and just to the main gates.The hill is steep and I found it quite hard work on a hot day, but the great views at the top make it well worth the effort.Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Waynesworld1
reviews.title: Worth the effort
reviews.content: Did this as part of a motorbike tour with Tommy' tours. Was amazing and if you can do the 500 steps worth the effort as the views and picture opportunities are endless.

reviews.author: Laurens
reviews.title: Enjoying the fantastic view on top of the mountain
reviews.content: In the early morning, we climbed the mountain to enjoy the views during a less crowed moment of the day. We were lucky we were there during low season so we could enjoy the views even more and the silence. When arriving at this place, a lot of people will stop you and try to force you to park on their parking for quite a lot of money. If you are able to get something off the price, then you should park there, else you should continue driving until the entrance. A lot of tourists come here, so that is why. The cave was flooded during our visit so we cannot review that cave.

reviews.author: LienTP
reviews.title: A beautiful tourist destination and should come to Ninh Binh
reviews.content: The view from above to the rice fields and the river and rocky system of Ninh Binh. The view is very beautiful and wonderful. If you come in the summer from may to July, you will meet beautiful and large Lotus ponds and ripe rice fields.Climb up 2 peaks about 200m to see panoramic view of Tam Coc. Do not miss this attraction.Weekends are crowded with many people

reviews.author: Claire D
reviews.title: Climb at mua caves
reviews.content: It was an intense climb but so worth it for the amazing view of the river and surrounding areas. It was well worth the trek to the summit.

reviews.author: Omid k
reviews.title: Beautiful place
reviews.content: Lovely place ,, lovely sights , if you go to nin bin i recommend you to see mua caves ,,, you must go up in the mountain with hard stairs ,, i think best time to see mua caves is on the eveving and sun set time

reviews.author: brendan_c130788
reviews.title: Walk up Mua Cave steps to view point
reviews.content: Excellent view point. 500 steps. Hard work but amazing views at top. Do not stop at any parking until you get right to the end of the road (at the mua cave eco resort). Some of the people can be aggressive trying to get you to park at their bit. Just cycle round them. Here it is 5000D for a bicycle. 150k D to enter. Well worth it

reviews.author: KereruHugger
reviews.title: Mua Caves. Lovely view but beware of the parking aggression
reviews.content: As others have reported on trip advisor, please be careful when visiting Hang Mua. We had not read the reviews and were just exploring by bike off the advice of our home stay who had not mentioned any parking fees, so we were completely unprepared for the parking horrors that followed.As soon as you turn down the road to the Mua Caves and view point you start getting harassed by locals telling you to park at their spot. The drama started for us about one third of the way down when a local blocked our path and shouted that we must park there. We could see other bikes and scooters at the end, so we stepped around him and kept going despite getting shouted and whistled at. Once we got just outside the entrance a few other visitors confirmed that they had been told there was no need to pay (as you have to pay an entrance cost also) and that the parking fees were a scam. So we tried to park our bikes and another local came up and started shouting at us, demanding payment of 20k each. We said, no, no, payment is not required. He got extremely aggressive and grabbed our 12 year old son’s bike and started marching off with it. My son grabbed it back, at which point the local went and got a large chain threatening to lock our bikes if we didn’t pay. My husband stared filming with his phone as it was all so aggressive, and the local gestured grabbing the phone off him and smashing it on the ground. At this point another local motioned to us that we could go inside the grounds and park there. According to information the other visitors had, this was free! It might have been once, but not anymore!Once inside, an official looking local then demanded payment of 5k each. Because we had been so bullied up to this point, and had been told that parking was free, we continued to try to communicate that the information we had was that parking is free. The official looking guy started shouting at us, standing very close and aggressively, then he stormed off to get another lock. By now it was not the money, just the overall way we were being treated and so we and the others all left on principle (it was very nice having company of the others during this very nasty incident). On our way back down the road, about 200m, there was a sign up saying free parking, so we all left our bikes there and they were perfectly safe (much to our relief). Finally, when we were headed out after visiting, another group of unsuspecting cyclists got stopped at the beginning of the road. We let them know that they did not have to stop there, and they could find free parking, and the local actually threw a stone at us. Fair enough if he were trying to make an honest living, but the entire road is riddled with very angry and aggressive people. On the whole, we are not sure that the views are worth running this gauntlet of anger (the cave certainly isn’t!).This was just so disappointing, the aggression and anger was beyond belief and like nothing we have experienced despite travelling through 5 different countries in Asia, and is so out of step with many other very kind people. We hope that something is done to sort it out, but in the meantime, the best we can do is warn you all, and maybe you can vote with your feet and give this site a miss.

reviews.author: Seana H
reviews.title: PARKING SCAM- Excellent views
reviews.content: Saw a lot of people struggling with this so I thought I’d write the review. Unlike other attractions in Ninh Binh where there is one designated parking spot, the entire lane leading up to Hang Mua is filled with private parking stands that charge varying prices. Drive all the way to the end. DO NOT stop for the man who will wave you down in the middle of the road. On the way in and out we saw him bullying tourists into his parking lot, lying to them and saying you couldn’t park farther down. He was very aggressive and (naturally) pretty pissed when we told the people he was harassing to keep going.Even though this soured our experience a bit, the views here are spectacular and worth the effort. Amazing to take in the natural landscape and walk the dragons tail up the left side. One other minor annoyance is that they do charge for the WC here. You’d think it’d be included in the ticket price, but apparently not.

reviews.author: MaximeLecl
reviews.title: Great point of view! Easy to reach!
reviews.content: The panoramic point of view is really beautiful and easy to reach (less than 500  steps, they can be done under 10 minutes one way if you have stamina!).We went to the summit around lunchtime and the stream of people seriously decreased.Our guess is that tours from Hanoi go to the restaurant around noon so we had a relatively peaceful hike to the summit. Parking is 10.000 VND for a motorbike.Drive until ticket counter.Sunset time must be crowded.We did not see the cave as we were told they were just ok.

reviews.author: Megan and Allan
reviews.title: Worth the hike up the stairs
reviews.content: We cycled through the rice paddies from Tam Coc. Straight to the ticket office, pay for bike parking, all bikes are numbered. Beautiful views from the top. Stairs get a bit slippery where they are black and shiny

reviews.author: Melanie B
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: The view from the top is wonderful. The climb up is long, kids had no issue and raced ahead. We climbed the steps to the dragon and the pagoda. Both were great. Take water and a fan as it gets quite hot and many steps to climb. Stairs are a bit in even so wear sneakers or good walking shoes unlike my husband who wore thongs, he did it fine but said sneakers would have been much easier. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: Alice Looi
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: The view on the top of Mua Cave is beautiful! But the climbing up, though was said to be 500 steps, was like 1000 steps for me, as some of the stairs are quite high.. The entrance to Mua Cave is via the Ecolodge... Looks like a nice place to stay in.. And there's a large lotus flowers pond which can be viewed from high up on Mua Cave too. Fascinating! Overall it's worthwhile to go.

reviews.author: Eden V
reviews.title: A challenging experience
reviews.content: We have about 486 stairs, the stairs are as normal as it sounds, but this is not very difficult either. The stair climbing is worth the view at the end of the hill.

reviews.author: Marie
reviews.title: A bit physical but definitely worth it!
reviews.content: Amazing landscapes once you arrive at the top. Even on the way everything is beautiful. Quite a lot of stairs to climb but it's worth it!

reviews.author: ernur
reviews.title: Because it is Ninh Binh Province
reviews.content: İt is easy to reach from Hanoi. You may try daily tours or overnight at this place. Our choice was second one and spend 2 days. Mua caves is the top place of Ninh Binh. You may see all mountains, rivers and boats easily. The weather forecast is not good for this areq. Because of micro-climate, you may face with sunny weather even if there is thunderstorm at forecast.  500 steps up and it is worth to see the beatuy of whole area. September is also good choice for visiting. Stable weather, green rice paddies, less humidity. Stop thinking and just let go this place.

reviews.author: Hol
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: You cannot miss this when in the area. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit. There are a lot of steep steps to climb in heat so it may not suit some. I suggest like us you arrive at 8.30/9am whist it's still cool and you beat the crowds. However even at that time there was a bit of posing and 'photoshoots' going on clogging up the view points. Dread to think what it might be like later in the day with more tourists. That aside it's a wonderful spot and worth the steps for the fantastic views.

reviews.author: extravelagent
reviews.title: Incredible views from the top; wear shoes (not slippers)
reviews.content: Got to Hang Mua via a little side road from Trang An grottoes, Even surprised that we got there. You would think that such a popular attraction they would pave the road to the attraction but it was an experience trying to navigate the dirt road and pot holes. Once again you need to pay for motorbike parking (30k I think) and to get in costs 50K (I 100K I can't remember really).
