Once you pay you cut thru this funky entrance area that has a bar and coffee /billard place. We beelined it to the start of the hike since it was about to rain. A word to the wise, wear sneakers that day you go up. It was drizzling and our slippers did not grip and when they say 500 steps, they aren't "normal" steps; they are semi-cemented, super high steps so it felt a lot harder (and we are hikers).We did the path on the left and not the one to the pagoda (right) as that one apparently had loose steps ans we didn't want to chance it with slippers. The left path led to the higher view and the dragon and we wanted to see that. It also had a view to the river behind the mountain. It's an awesome view of the city and the surroundings once you reach the top. I think they are still working on the steps so beware the tools and machinery just laid across the path (this is Vietnam!). Definitely worth a stop on your motorbike day in that area. And try not to stay too late as you still need to navigate the unpaved road on the way out! And when leaving, look up into the mountains and you might see the white goats like we did! SO cool!

reviews.author: vikvijayan
reviews.title: Great view - shame about the ‘Gramers
reviews.content: Early start to enjoy the serenity and beauty of the Lying Dragon’s peak - reached it at about 6:20 am. The lovely view was slightly marred by the four drones buzzing noisy around the peak by millennials seeking the ultimate Instagram shot. A pity - but I guess that’s the way the world works now. Still worth the trip, even if its to do your part and throw some of the plastic trash into bins. There are bins up there and along the way. Why people can’t use them is beyond me.

reviews.author: Jolly traveler
reviews.title: Panoramic
reviews.content: I arrived early in the morning which is actually the perfect time to climb. Take your time, climb up both summits, and then come down to enjoy the lovely gardens at the foot of the climb. The panoramic view from the peak is absolutely stunning.

reviews.author: Canary289
reviews.title: Amazing view from the top
reviews.content: This place is one of the most instagrammable  places in Vietnam. The cave itself is nothing special but the view from the top is stunning. Climb 500 stone steps to reach its top and enjoy the uninterrupted view of the sky and ricefield underneath. To have the best photo, come here during harvest season (may-june). Entrance ticket is 100,000vnd(5$).

reviews.author: Prince_Brand999
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Great to spend cca 2 hours - the climb to the viewpoint was easier then I expected, great view on the area. The cave itself was small, there are much more beautiful ones in the area.

reviews.author: Jennifer
reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.content: Loved this location!  Stayed on site at the Mua Caves Ecolodge which gave access early in morning before crowds arrived.  Enjoyed the early morning hike.  Beautiful views from top. Was fun to people watch as crowds arrived - those who were serious hikers and those all dressed up for the perfect picture.

reviews.author: Timmy C
reviews.title: The earlier the better
reviews.content: We started our hike up the 500 steps at 6.30am, a much better time to do this than the heat of the day. And an added bonus is that there aren't a lot of people around either - the tour buses hadn't arrived yet. Take plenty of water, stop frequently for the views, it's worth it. Just a note if you are arriving by bike/scooter - DON'T take the first parking area you are offered as it's quite a walk to the entrance, go as far as you can towards the entrance, - you will have to pay anyway so why not get as close as you can. 10,000 VND for scooter, 5,000 VND for bicycle. Actual caves not anything special.

reviews.author: k2711
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: We climbed the 500 steps to the highest point which was a total killer but worth it for the unbelievable views.

reviews.author: Bethan S
reviews.title: Beautiful views at sunset - but getting pricey and busy.
reviews.content: Cycled to the caves from Tam Coc, mistakenly expecting a 20k entry free and free bike parking. PARKING AT THE SITE IS NO LONGER FREE. You can avoid the people telling you to park with them for free/for a higher fee, but you will still have to pay at the site itself - it seems they've caught wind of more opportunities to profit. I went and asked at the ticket counter for the site (entry is now 100k per person) if it was right that we paid for parking, and she assured us we had to pay.We made the climb at sunset, and it was a stunning view, but honestly surprised there wasn't an injury/someone falling - people were climbing over each other trying to get a spot to sit/to take photos, and it was just so busy. Definitely would recommend going as early in the day as possible to avoid crowds.

reviews.author: DeerDuBois
reviews.title: Amazing viewpoint with a dragon! But beware!!
reviews.content: Go for the viewpoint on top of the steep 500 steps. Amazing view! Price 100k VND.But be aware: if you come by (motor)bike, do NOT let yourself be tricked by the annoying guy with his whistle at 300m of the entrance. He will (violently) try to make you stop and pay for parking. Drive further until your are in the walls of the entry near the ticketbooth and park there for free. Also be aware for people on the way there giving fake directions to lead you to their restaurant or shop!

reviews.author: Ratheeshtravi
reviews.title: Birds eye view of tam coc
reviews.content: It takes 500 steps to reach the top, but trust me it’s worth! It may be bit difficult to reach the top with kids. Avoid the climb during the noon time and try to reach there only after 4 when the sun is not too hot. Mua cave is located next to a resort so there are many shops and restaurants available nearby. Carry a bottle of water with you!

reviews.author: Karen E
reviews.title: 500 steps to a spectacular view
reviews.content: We did this on a tour.  The steps are quite steep and we arrived just before lunch and it was quite night before there was a lot of rain so steps were a bit slippery on the way down.  Once at the top you have to wrestle with the crowds to get a photo with the dragon.  Not a lot of room for very many people to be there at once.  The view is awesome and well worth the climb.  You can see why they call it Halong bay on land. There is a couple of nice tourist shops where we could actually look and not get harassed.  Would have been nice to have the time to climb the other peak to get a good photo shot of the main climb.

reviews.author: Ashley M
reviews.title: Mua Caves Beautiful / careful with scams
reviews.content: Once you are at the top of the mountain the view is amazing! The dragon and the statue are not as impressive from closer view as they are in the photos from far distance but, it is worth it the experience of climbing the stairs and getting there. At the entrance there are a bunch of things to buy and a restaurant, the whole place beautifully decorated and well maintained. You can park a scooter in the parking of the location for 10.000VND. Pay attention that the route to get to the location is basically one narrow road with several parking lots and very aggressive sellers. While driving they try to call your attention standing in the middle of the road demanding that you have to park with them. They charge more, and you will end up walking all the way to the entrance of the location unnecessarily. Better safe your energy for the stairs.

reviews.author: Travellingt1m
reviews.title: Do not get tricked by fake parkings!
reviews.content: Do not get tricked by the fake "parkings" along the small road to the Mua site. They act very aggressively to get you to their parking, acting like officials with strong hand gestures and whistles. Just ignore then and continue driving until the ticket office of Mua entrance. There you can park your motorbike for VND 10,000. Entrance to Mua is VND 100,000 per person.The climb was steep and hot, but much worth it as the view from the top is stunning!

reviews.author: tclm1971
reviews.title: Steep climbing but we did it with our 2 year old
reviews.content: We embarked on the climb with the advice - it’s probably too hard for your child... but we did it.It might have taken us a little longer then the youngsters  but we climbed up with our daughter. The steps at times were as high as her waist but she persisted... with a few tricky bits where she needed to be carried. What we saw at the to was worth every step.I don’t know why people complain about the few dollars it costs to climb this monument... in my eyes the views weed priceless !

reviews.author: Jan.parker523NY
reviews.title: 100VND
reviews.content: The scenery on the mountain is beautiful, but there's nothing at the top of the mountain. I don't know why the tickets are so expensive

reviews.author: ExplorerGabor
reviews.title: Steep walk that’s worth it
reviews.content: The views from the top of both peaks are stunning.  Yes there are 500 steps and they are very steep.  The steps to the pagoda summit are steep and high with a narrow path.  Space at the top near the pagoda is very limited.  The path to the summit with the dragon is also steep though the path is wide.  We went at 3pm and it was still very hot.  Took us 45mins to climb and descend with a break at the top.  The views in each direction are amazing.  Lots of people posing for photos, it’s clearly an Instagram spot.

reviews.author: Ramesh
reviews.title: Actually view was unbeliever
reviews.content: Its was a amazing experience beautiful nature and cold wind and enjoyable moments incredible views on the top of the mua caves we has enjoyed here so we are recommend

reviews.author: Roy L
reviews.title: Lovely view from the top
reviews.content: Incredibly crowded in the late morning. But views were spectacular overlooking the limestone hills and green rivers. Take the left fork nearer to the top to reach the stone dragon at the higher peak. Takes abit of guts to climb out onto the dragon but it affords you some peace and quiet to take in the scenery away from the crowds at the pavilion with the goddess of mercy statue.Highly recommended

reviews.author: Ela D
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: Absolutely stunning view. Takes 500 steps to reach the peak but absolutely worth it. We went there for the the sunset, which I highly  recommend! The ticket costs 100000 dong per person.

reviews.author: happy tourism vietnam🇻🇳😊🙂
reviews.title: Traveling
reviews.content: Nice place.  Wild  Sophisticated structure.Note to the Mua Cave: do not wear high heels.  Should wear comfortable clothes.  An umbrella or hat is needed.  Because rain and sunshine are not foretold.

reviews.author: Metti_65
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: Even at 38 degrees and high humidity, the effort is rewarded with a magnificent view over the dry Halong Bay and the beautiful landscape. It is especially recommended to make the ascent at sunset.

reviews.author: Michelle and Iz... C
reviews.title: Magical views
reviews.content: The climb up the steps was a little tough given the heat 🥵but the views at the top made it worth it 🇻🇳

reviews.author: Chi epprn Teponler
reviews.title: Incredible trip
reviews.content: We would such a great time looking at the Mua caves, it's a relatively low excursion and also the a number of the suggestions you receive an opportunity to access are amazing. The landscapes are breathtaking. You will get to explore caves from the protection of the boat of yours, with a seasoned boatman to point you through, our boatman was very dextrous and was really rowing the oars of his with the foot of his! The people which point you on the boats don't seem to chat a good deal of English but which might have been just the boatman of ours. We did the excursion with the aged parents of mine so regrettably didn't get to do the trek almost as the fantastic views - truly gutted we missed out on this because the images seem to be impressive! I definitely would suggest this specific journey!

reviews.author: dream
reviews.title: Fit for hiking
reviews.content: If You want to find a place for hiking.Mua Cave is a best place for that in Ninh Binh.From there you can see a whole of ecologe view and field.Its so beautiful

reviews.author: Maisie L
reviews.title: Mia caves
reviews.content: We went to mua caves  claimed  all the steps  great views  from the  top  the stairs  wasn't  to bad to climb   when you got further  to the top they  get steeper   we went for 830.in the  morning so wasn't  to  hot and not many people  so that  was  better

reviews.author: DaisyM777
reviews.title: You need to come really early to enjoy this place properly and to avoid the heat and “Instagram crowds”
reviews.content: Unfortunately we arrived there around 11am,it was almost 40C and so humid that everyone was drenched in sweat.Our tour guide rushed us and gave us only 45 minutes which was extremely short time to even appreciate the surroundings,not mention the climbing.So we used our 45 minute “”allowance”.You have two paths,one is 487 steps and it takes you to the dragon statue and another one(easier)is 400 steps.We took the harder path that takes you to the dragon statue.The steps itself were okay,nothing unusual for this type of a climb but it was the hit and humidity that was killing everyone on that day.Once you reach the end of the steps,you need to climb the steep rocks to reach the dragon.The rocks are slippery and sharp so it’s the best to wear walking shoes or trainers.Dragon is impressive I must say.It was very busy when we went there,bunch of exhausted people,people taking wedding pictures,a lot of noise and already small unsafe space around the dragon was packed with people.It was very difficult to even take proper picture because of the amount of “Instragramers” looking for the perfect spot was uncountable.I would like to visit Mua Caves again,but this time without organised tour and to be there for at least 7am in the morning to fully enjoy the area and the views.

reviews.author: Ling Chen
reviews.title: 景觀優美，售票處旁可以停車
reviews.content: You can parking inside, bike 5K, motobike 10K, car 20K. The shop stop you and charge the parking fee 15K, cheating!By almost 550 steps, you can get on the top. Bring the water!外面的攤商攔車，並收取15K，令人討厭，售票處旁邊能停車，比外面便宜。上山的階梯約550階，左邊能看到tam coc一部分及龍的所在，右邊則是能遠挑龍及另一面景色，如果要選擇一邊，我會走左邊。頂部沒有攤商，應該帶水上去。門票要100K，但廁所仍舊要收費，越南各處好像都是如此。

reviews.author: Kusovka
reviews.title: Stunning Cave
reviews.content: Can you imagine to be in a big wonderful cave alone? Here your dreams come true. If you are able to survive 2 kilometers to the top of the mountain in the unreal heat and humidity, you will be rewarded by a stunning cave where you could be alone. No guide, no restriction, only you. Don't forget a flashlight, at least on your phone. It is possible that during your cave tour the light turns off...

reviews.author: Hannah H
reviews.title: Some of the most beautiful views in Vietnam
reviews.content: A very very hot hike up two huge peaks, to see absolutely spectacular views across the mountains. In hindsight we wish we had taken the boat from Tam Coc to the caves and back however we only had a day so we didn't have a chance to do this.

reviews.author: DerriQ
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Visited here yesterday at about 3pm. It was soooo hot and humid so made it a very hard climb. The view was nice but it was very busy up top which made it hard to get a good photo.  Lovely place with lots of spots to buy a refreshing drink of cold water thank goodness!

reviews.author: Angie
reviews.title: Good climb, better view at the top.
reviews.content: Climb was pretty arduous because of the unforgiving sun. But the view is rewarding and beautiful.Would be good to pack some food, and then hike up, stay there for awhile and enjoy your food with the view. Cave entrance was small and don’t think you can explore much into the caves.

reviews.author: Hang Do
reviews.title: Amazing scenery
reviews.content: Mua Cave in the northern province of Ninh Binh has been popular to domestic and foreign visitors thanks to the picturesque scenery of the surrounding area seen from its top. When coming to Mua Cave, you will have opportunity to try your endurance when climbing to the top of the mountain through 486 stone steps. From the top of the mountain, we can admire the whole beauty of Tam Coc area with immense, green rice fields.Mua Cave is located at the foot of Mua Mountain in the ecotourism community in Khe Dau Ha village, Ninh Xuan, Hoa Lu and Ninh Binh communes. To get here, you can follow Highway 1A to Ninh Binh city and turn to Trang An or Tam Coc, then you will see a sign leading to Hang Mua tourist resort. You can travel by coach, there are some coach companies such as Minh Long or Hoang Long buses, they have high quality of coach operators. Or if you want to travel by taxi, you can book a car of Dichung Taxi, Mai Linh Taxi or Minh Long Taxi. This place is known as the "muse of Tam Coc" or "Great wall of Vietnam" with the majestic scenery of the peaks, poetic view of golden rice fields or charming towers on the top of the mountain.Beside the beautiful scenery, the highlight of this tourist destination is the road leading to the top of Mua Mountain, which is modeled after the Great Wall of China with nearly 500 stone steps. From the top of Mua Mountain, visitors can admire the whole beautiful scenery of Tam Coc area, famous scenic spot in Ninh Binh. Legend has it that the Tran Kings used to visit the area to watch the imperial maids sing and dance, giving the area its name, Mua or ‘dancing’.At the center of the relic is a large artificial lake, flanked by shady green trees creating an extremely airy space and sweeping views of the sacred mountain. On the top of the mountain is a statue of the Bodhisattva with eyes looking down to the ancient capital.You can stay right here then hike or cycle to nearby locations such as Tam Coc, Bai Dinh Pagoda, Trang An or Van Long Lagoon.

reviews.author: MexicoSaran
reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.content: Very good experience and had fun by 500 steps hills top. It seems no safety in top. I am Saravanan from Chennai India

reviews.author: Janex_9
reviews.title: Amazing View from the Top
reviews.content: We cycled here from Tam Coc early one morning, arriving about 6.45am. It was quiet and a great time to be out and about. It was a trek to the top of the hill and I don’t think I have ever sweated that much but it was worth it for the wonderful, panoramic views. Spectacular. The park or what ever it is at the foot of the hill is rather odd but we walked straight through that. We didn’t look at the caves. My only criticism is regarding the rubbish all up the steps and all over the top. An entry fee is charged so please use some of it to sort out the unsightly rubbish! Don’t spoil this beautiful place by ignoring the rubbish!  And take your rubbish away with you when you visit, don’t just throw it on the ground. The one thing about Vietnam that I just don’t understand at all.

reviews.author: philtechie
reviews.title: Worthwhile visit if you don't mind a climb and over touristic locations
reviews.content: We were looking forward to visiting mainly for the climb and promised views. My first impression was that it is overly commercialised. The entry fee is a bit high for Vietnam at 200000 vnd each. Immediately as you walk through the entrance you walk past many stalls, cafes and restaurants which made it feel a little like Disney. The climb was quite tough with uneven steps, and made harder by the heat. It was quite busy with visitors when we visited, around 4pm on a late August day. With no wind we were soon dripping with sweat so I'm glad it was our last stop before returning to the hotel. The  cave was interesting but not exceptional. Lovely view from the top, but lots of people about taking selfies, so don't expect a magical experience!

reviews.author: Adventurer184158
reviews.title: Hang Mua
reviews.content: This area is about 115km from Hanoi or 2hr drive in moderate traffic. It is a good locale for trekking activity.  At the top (approx 500steps) of Mua peak, there is an  impressive panoramic view of the surrounding  limestone hills, Ngo Giang river & rice fields in Tam Coc & Trang An & Ninh Binh. Entrance is 100,000vnd.As for the cave, I did not see any substantial caverns on both the hills except at the foot of the hill where the stairs begins. There is a small hole at the side of the hill. Probably good for sunrise and sunset photoshoots  with 360° views.

reviews.author: Travelling_Guy38
reviews.title: Hot
reviews.content: Climbed in a storm and was quite something watching the storm roll in. Views are amazing bug it is quite a climb in the heat. Watch for the parking scams with very aggressive parking attendants.

reviews.author: Anna H
reviews.title: Sooo many steps!)))
reviews.content: Beatiful place with amazing views...I gave up climbing half way as it was raining and steps became slippery..but still enjoyed it a lot!!

reviews.author: Dean P
reviews.title: Good view
reviews.content: It has an amazing view. But I think it would be a little more expensive for the ticket. Overall its worth for a nice view

reviews.author: Elias
reviews.title: Avoid the crazy man at the first parking spot
reviews.content: The views are very beautiful and it's worth the walk. If you come by motorbike/bike, avoid the parking scams. Don't go any other route than the one with the signs to get there. Don't stop by the first men who tells you to stop. It's a scam, you have to pay more money and have to walk much further. He tried to attack us with rocks, totally insane guy. Just ignore them and drive all the way to the big gate/wall. You will know when you get there!

reviews.author: Gerald
reviews.title: A spectacular view!
reviews.content: Most likely among the favorite spots of mine in the province. Whether or not the climate is not shocking, the mist provides many atmospheres. Would suggest getting on a motorbike and seeing - it is just fifteen minutes outside Tam Coc.

reviews.author: Yellowhummingbird
reviews.title: Spectacular views from top
reviews.content: From the bottom up you can expect climbing 450 steep steps. Don’t do it if you are not in good physical shape. The climb is definitely worth it as the view from top is spectacular.you can see the rock formations and the river winding through The Valley. It’s amazing. On the other side you look down on rice fields and in the far distance you see Ninh Bin.

reviews.author: Martina S
reviews.title: The best experience
reviews.content: The view is outstanding. You should take a good shoes  cause steps are very steep. The best place to spend the sunset at. I wouldnt recomend to climb the steps elderly people or pregnant women.

reviews.author: sabine.andrey
reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.content: That's amazing mountain & good destination. It's a bit hard to finish this climbing up tour but the view from the top of island was exceptional!

reviews.author: J3nnE
reviews.title: Stunning view point
reviews.content: Beautiful walk up to the top to see the lying dragon. Absolutely soaked in sweat in 36 degree heat in august but definitely worth it for the beautiful view at the top. As for the caves themseleves there is not a lot to see and is not worth going for that. But the exhausting walk definitely is!! Few spots along the way to stop off for refreshments if needed.

reviews.author: Ebrahim A
reviews.title: amazing location for photography
reviews.content: amazing location for photography. its a bot hard to climbing but when you arrive on the top you can see really amazing views of mountains and river and you can take a good photos

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.title: Beautiful views but watch out for aggressive locals
reviews.content: The Mua Cave view point offers breathtaking views of the Vietnamese countryside. It’s a strenuous hike to the top so make sure to not choose the hottest day of the week. Once at the top, there is a little hut that offers some shade and you can climb around the dragon statue for some cool pictures. Since the top is quite small it can get busy. We paid an entrance fee of 100,000 per person. Oh Although the viewpoint is highly recommendable, getting there was not a very pleasant experience. We came on a scooter and as soon as we reached the road the leads to the cave there were locals aggressively trying to make us park at their spots. We weren’t aware of this beforehand so we made the mistake of stopping at one of these place. After signaling that we wanted to move on to the end of the road, the lady started to scream at us in Vietnamese and whistled at or faces until we finally managed to get around her. Other locals jumped in front of our scooted and tried to stop it by pushing against it from the front. The best way of getting through this road is probably to keep on driving and shaking your head/beeping at any local who tries to stop you.

reviews.author: Martijn J
reviews.title: Nice place for quick visit
reviews.content: The cave it self was not very jnteresting. The climb to the top of the mountain was exausting in 35 plus degrees but very rewarding. Beautifull views from above

reviews.author: Parker Thomas
reviews.title: Best views of Vietnam.
reviews.content: Amazing experience to see the views from the top and touch the dragon for a blessings. As far as parking be kind to the locals and they rent the spaces and are only trying to make a buck to live. Be polite and just keep driving inside the gate. I had no problems. The parking issue you will finds at all venues so just always go to the venue and it’s a sure bet.

reviews.author: FreddyDalgaard
reviews.title: Mua Caves
reviews.content: Definitely worth the walk up the 500 or so steps. I would recommend going up for sunset as it is much cooler and the views are spectacular. I gained entry for free as I stayed at the ecolodge at the bottom of the mountain however, I would definitely pay the entry fee. It was worth the time and money.

reviews.author: Nguyen Ngoc Phong ( Windy )
reviews.title: Amazing Viewpiont for Hanoi photography tours feel :
reviews.content: Amazing Viewpiont for Hanoi photography tours feel , that is real feeling which i just finish my journey to discover Mua Cave and lying Dragon with 8 my friends from Spain. even now it is not ricefield season , i still  take a lot of nice photo from the top of the Mua mountian , Windy really enjoy so much , I will suggest for my friends for sure .now you can see my picture from the Mua cave mountain by Windy photography :

reviews.author: Stephanie V
reviews.title: Tourist trap and agressive scam parking guys
reviews.content: Nice view on the top but definetely not worth the money. The fake parking guys where very agressive and forced us to park on their parking which we refused, later when we came back from our hike we saw that they destroyed our motorbike.

reviews.author: molly.markland
reviews.title: Great view
reviews.content: It's very hard to climb up to the top in a very hot Day. I just can do one point but the view & atmosphere from the top was excellent. A must do!

reviews.author: Charlotte
reviews.title: Great view from the top, terrible caves
reviews.content: The fact that you have to pay and also pay for parking lost this a star. The caves aren't worth the trip, but the climb really is! There is a beautiful view from the top if you don't sweat to death before you get there. Go early to avoid tourists and the heat

reviews.author: LinhVu
reviews.title: Worth to visit
reviews.content: From the top of Hang Mua we can have a wide panoramic view over the Ninh Binh valley, which is stunning as can be shown in my photos here. However during summer time it’s better to climb up there before 10am to avoid the extreme sun heat. Wear proper footwear too coz the steps are pretty much not in order & quite slippery even on sunny days. Spend 90min in here is enough.

reviews.author: Isabel B
reviews.title: View is great at the top!!
reviews.content: Definitely worth doing if you are in the Tam Coc area. It’s 100,000 VD per person which I think is on the expensive side just for a viewpoint but we paid it anyway. The view from the top is beautiful. There are also a few caves to check out near the bottom which were cool too. Drinks etc are expensive so bring drinks from outside. Also the path you take towards the caves, there are a lot of locals shouting/using whistles to get your attention to make you park in their parking spots - these are a lot more expensive. The correct parking is at the bottom of the path, and we paid 5000 VD per bike.

reviews.author: Garry A
reviews.title: viewpoint
reviews.content: this area is known as mua caves but actually just a very small uninteresting cave , its actually a viewpoint that does give some very nice views from the top , around 500 steps to reach the top and many of the steps are quite high , 100,000 dong entry around 4$ , if you drive a motorbike or car there yourself once you enter the road that leads to the entrance there is a guy that offers parking right at the beginning of the road but this is quite a long walk from the entrance , DONT park here ,continue driving  along the road to the entrance,  there will be another 2 or 3 people trying to get you to park in their place along the entrance road but ignore them all and drive right to the entrance where there is parking available to the right side of the entrance , 15000 to park motorbike but once you have finished the climb you will be glad that you parked right next to the entrance .Before going to this cave i read a few reviews that said some of the guys that want you to park in their place will stand in front of the bike to stop you  passing and they can get very angry if u dont park in their place but i didnt see this , my advice would be that if anyone tries to stop you before the entrance DO NOT STOP , just continue to the entrance and park to the right side of the entrance

reviews.author: behzrings
reviews.title: Hot visit with a great view
reviews.content: We had a pleasant stay. With a great view after 15 hot minutes up the mountain. We cane with private car and had no issues with unpleasant experiences as described by other users

reviews.author: goingwhereicanwhenican
reviews.title: Not a hike but nice view anyway
reviews.content: The trip out to Mua Cave wasn't as bad as a I thought, the 2 hour car ride was bearable.  We were told we'd be hiking.. which is not what I'd call the steps up to the top of the cave.  It was about 500 steps and there was a concession stand mid-way for those who needed something cold to drink.  The view from the top was nice but I wasn't blown away.  The area was very touristy with weird lights and lanterns and fake ponds which made it a bit cheesy... The cave itself was very boring. You couldn't go very far in and it was described as "half man-made and half natural".  There was nothing to see in the cave.  It was nice going out to see Mua Caves, Tam Coc and Hoa Lu as a day trip from Hanoi after seeing all the attractions in the city. I saw some home stays in the area... I would not stay here over night.  There is nothing to do and it would definitely be boring.  Also, visit Halong Bay before making the trip out to do the Mua Caves/Tam Coc/Hoa Lu day trip.

reviews.author: Ying
reviews.title: Beautiful view, not worth the scam for parking though
reviews.content: The view was beautiful, but go early in the morning, or when the sun starts to set, because there will be no shade to cover yourself when climbing onto the Mua Caves. The view is nice with the ricefields and people climb on the dragons which is cool. When it is cloudy, you would not be able to see much of the view. The parking people are quite aggressive, just keep driving until you see the actual sign, and park as close as you can to the entrance, just keep driving. Before the climb, there was a lot of fake grass and construction going on, kind of faking the authenticity of the place and having very random and also a bit scary statues.

reviews.author: Nick A
reviews.title: Was threatened by locals with STICKS, CHAINS and KNIVES
reviews.content: We rode our bike past the scamming locals who want you to park at their parking stop. One of the guys at the very end kicked our bike and hit my girlfriend on her leg as we were driving by. When confronted, ten other locals jumped out with sticks, knives and chains. All of that happened in front of other tourists. DO NOT SUPPORT VIOLENT  LOCALS. We did end up climbing to the top despite the incident. Big mistake, should have just turned around and left. Even without that terrible experience, the site is not worth the visit that much, there are way more beautiful sites in Northern Vietnam, plus the people are nicer. After this incident and what I read online from other tourists, I am never coming back to this country. It is way different from all other South East Asian countries we have visited, where this type of behavior can happen, but is not the norm.

reviews.author: Simona D
reviews.title: Do not support these crazy violent people who scam tourists!
reviews.content: This experience put the cherry on top of this already not that pleasant journey around Vietnam. The locals hit me and my boyfriend and threatened us with a knife, a chain and iron rod. They are completely insane. They do not even talk to you, they shout in Vietnamese and demand money . This is NOT how you treat foreign visitors. I will not be returning to Vietnam, I wish I could change my ticket to leave earlier even. They could have put my boyfriend in a hospital or worse. They have no regards for societal norms, human interaction or the law.

reviews.author: tomtomnor
reviews.title: Parking scammers still active
reviews.content: Please ignore them. They look profesional with their flutes and vest and really are aggressive. But a beautifull place.

reviews.author: Patel96
reviews.title: Beautiful stay
reviews.content: We stayed here for 3 nights and it was beautiful! Rooms had AC and we were right at the bottom of the mountain. Not too noisy with the property open to the public.

reviews.author: Jenna Sinead
reviews.title: Please be aware of the extremely aggressive man forbidding you to go past him!
reviews.content: I cannot stress enough how dangerous the locals are on the road leading up to Mua Cave. My partner and I had a great morning at the Trang An Boat tour and we were so excited to head up the 500 steps to see the incredible scenery surrounding Tam Coc. As we arrived we were met with a local man running straight in front of our motorbike screaming and blowing a yellow whistle demanding we were to stop and pay him for parking. The man then  grabbed my arm pulling me from the bike. I was in total shock as to what had just happened and completely refused to pay him as I could clearly see multiple free parking signs ahead. I was also told Mua Cave had free parking which was still another 300m down the road, so knew it was a scam. The man continued to blow on his whistle, hold onto our bike and scream in our faces that he was not allowing us to go past. My partner and I were not giving this man any money and decided to park our bike at a lovely family restaurant a little further away. I have added a blurry photo of the man so so you can avoid being attacked. He is wearing the checked black and white coat.

reviews.author: Jack L
reviews.title: PARKING ATTENDANT SUPER AGGRESSIVE!
reviews.content: Absolute dampener on such an amazing time in Ninh Binh. My partner and I arrived around 3pm to start the trek up the Mua Cave mountain when we were abruptly stopped by a man acting to be an official parking attendant. I initially thought he was trying to scam us as I could see loads more parking signs beyond his stupid flailing arms and that harsh blow of his yellow whistle that could’ve deafened people in HCMC 1000 kilometres away! All jokes aside, he began to get even more aggressive with us when I told him that we weren’t paying and tried to move past. He grabbed my partners arm which resulting in her almost falling off the bike. Somehow I managed to remain calm and turn the bike around as I didn’t want to put my partner in a bad situation. We found a restaurant further back with free parking and left our bike there which was completely safe. I hope to god this guy gets his comeuppance by someone and tastes the pavement. FYI the guy works at the sign that says BÃI GÙI XE in red writing on the right hand side. I’d recommend exactly what someone has already mentioned in a review before. Gain some speed on your bike, blast the horn and don’t stop! Good luck!

reviews.author: Naomi
reviews.title: Amazing viewpoint
reviews.content: The viewpoint is very nice! It is quite a tough hike upwards (mostly because of the heat), so I recommend to do it early in the morning. We came with scooters and parked at the beginning of the street near a big sign with "parking mua cave", however, do not park here! You can drive all the way to the end to the ticketcounter and park over there (though several men try to stop you rather agressively)! But it saves you a walk and some money :)

reviews.author: Dan M
reviews.title: DANGER WHEN PARKING AT MUA CAVES PLEASE READ!!!! WE WERE ATTACKED BY SCAM PARKING ATTENDANT AFTER CHALLENGING HIM
reviews.content: We had a horrible experience at Mua CAVES. As you drive in a man in his 50's raced down on a moped to cajole us into the parking on the LHS as you enter. He issued a ticket and said 'yes free' 3 times. When I challenged him on this he turned agreesive and started screaming then took our moped and threw it out on the ground then when we drove down further he blocked us in then karate kicked the moped trying to break it. When we went to the 2nd place on the right (site B) they had a sign saying free parking so we parked outside there upon which the angry man returned to once again try to break our moped in front of us and threaten me. God only knows what he was venting. I asked the people we now parked with to call police or security. They said no police or security which concerned us. To be honest they seemed a bit scared of the guy too. This guy was mental. I'm a big guy and I stood firm but even I was thinking that next he will come out with a weapon to attack us. It ruined our experience. We didnt stop to visit the site in the end and moved on. Please, please if you are planning on going or read this and know someone who is, then warn them. Please re post this so that it stays at the top of the thread. One day he might really hurt someone. The management of the Mua Caves experience must know what is happening here. It's not the first story I've read about parking touts on reading through after my experience. Be warned. Be VERY CAREFUL. I hope TripAdvisor can make this a main thread so that something gets done. They need to know that it's going to affect their source of income and they'll soon change their methods.

reviews.author: ViktoriaGerzeny
reviews.title: It is a must to do!
reviews.content: We are glad we pick the Mua Caves as one of the places to see. It has a view of Trang An . It was our 2nd stop.

reviews.author: Patrick D
reviews.title: Mua Caves
reviews.content: Vietnamese name of Mua caves is Hang Múa (Hang  means cave and Múa - dancing ) According to a legend when the king Tran arrived at Hoa Lu to establish Thai Vi temple, the King was like visiting this cave for enjoying dancing performance by ladies  So for  that , the cave was named “Hang Mua"The cave is located in Khe Ha Village,  ( about 6km far from the city center) Mua Cave is lying at the foot of Mua mountain  A long stone staircase  .decorated on the stone with the lying Dragon  carved lead to the peak of the moutain and the altar  Quan Am (the Goddess of MercyThe 500 steps are quite rough because irregular up to the top of the mountainThere are huge karst mountains along with impressive landscape around,  one of the best views in Ninh BinhIt's really peaceful place early in the morning or in the late afternoon ... Late afternoon is also the best for the sunset .. By day , it's really  too much crowded Remember bringing a bottle of water, . Wearing simple and comfortable clothes and shoes that is suited to climb. It is a steep ascent  up with many of its uneven limestone steps ( expecially at the top point)The Mua Caves itself and the grounds surrounding it are beautiful but it a hard trek most of the time in wetland . I didn t  see a tourist during my  treks just a few locals . Most of the vistor climb the  steps up the Lying Dragon Mountain

reviews.author: haplo89
reviews.title: Nice hike to the top of a karst
reviews.content: At mua caves you can climb to the top of 2 karst mountains, the hike up is 500 steps and isn't all to difficult, however with the unrelenting hot sun it becomes a bit more of a challenge. Bring enough water and maybe an umbrella if you suffer heavy from the sun. The views on top are great. The Cave after which this location is named is not very impressive but a good place to cool down after your descent from the mountain.

reviews.author: Andyvjr
reviews.title: The climb up is rewarding... beware of parking scams
reviews.content: HYDRATE: Ok, it’s HOT And very humid in Vietnam so start this being well hydrated and keep hydrating during and after the climb. Start your climb as early as possible to avoid major heat exhaustion. PARKING: Beware of parking scams. They’re very aggressive tiny women that LITERALLY jump in front of your bike or motorbike blowing a whistle signaling you stop and directing you to their money pit parking lot. They seem official with their vests, whistles, and aggressive tactics to get you to stop. I read the warnings about this  on this forum and was so glad I did. A woman jumped in front of my bike and I ran her over and kept going while she cursed me out. I don’t take kindly to scammers. Many said the parking at the cave entrance was free but there was an official looking sign giving very cheap prices so don’t know if something changed or if it was a con job. Either way, for my bicycle it was only $500 VND which is a lot less than other parking places. It was hot and I wasn’t going to fight for .25 cents. THE CLIMB: def worth it. I didn’t see a mess like others reported. There was a trash can available  for your used plastic bottles. The view is worth the climb and the gauntlet of parking scam artist.

reviews.author: Lotuspearl
reviews.title: Not worth the climb if you are not very fit
reviews.content: We went in May and there were lots of bright colored caterpillars all along the way which freaked me out. Also the climb is tiring if you are not very fit.

reviews.author: CTR
reviews.title: A steep climb but well worth the effort
reviews.content: We hired bikes from our homestay and cycled the short, flat easy ride to the entrance of the site. We had to pay parking, but make sure you get as close as you can, don't stop at the first parking place and haggle the price down. Entry to the site is 100,000 (June 2019) and you climb over 500 steep steps. We went up at 5pm for sunset and despite relatively cloudy weather the light was amazing and even without the colours the views are amazing. Definitely recommend this place if you're in Tam Coc/Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Rhea-Dew
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: We stayed in the Ecolodge located right near the start of the climb. Only took an 1hr and half to climb up and see both sides. We took our time as it is very humid and hot, plenty of water needed and sun protection! There are some nice shady spots to stop and catch your breath and we were lucky enough to have a nice breeze up the top. We went up at about 8am. View was amazing, on the way down we were quite glad we were staying there so we could hop into a cold shower and an air conditioned room to cool off. The caves however, not as impressive. Not sure if they are planning on doing some more work on them to make it more of an attraction. We went into both that we could find and both were filed with water, one looked like they had built their own pool of some sort, but obviously people seem to come here for the climb and the Instagram picture!

reviews.author: manhchu
reviews.title: Best view of Tam coc
reviews.content: I and my friend visited Mua cave in May. It was stunning view. We took alot of nice photos. We have to walk up few hundreds meters. It was quite hard for lazy guy. But we can do it and you too. When we come on top of this site. It was open a wide nice and stunning view of Tam coc rice field. You should visit here in the rice time to have better view.Together with Mua cave you should visit Trang An riverIt worth to visit in Ninh Binh

reviews.author: Kimmiecarroll
reviews.title: Challenging hike but worth it!
reviews.content: I was worried about climbing the 500 steps, and it was indeed difficult, but oh so worth it!  Awesome views. The rocks right around the dragon are pretty jagged and steep and there isn't much room so we opted not to fight the crowd for the Instagram shot.

reviews.author: Sathilde
reviews.title: Nobody cares about the caves
reviews.content: We are here to climb to the dragon. It's high. It's hot. But you can do it. You will sweat. But everybody sweat. Let's have a sint toh after this!Good luck.

reviews.author: Tambonz
reviews.title: High place
reviews.content: Don't wear jandals or thongs on yer feet.Slippery as hell coming down the very steep stairs... All 580 of them. Quite wide too.Caves are OK.. Nothing to write home about.

reviews.author: Anna D
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: Initially I was very scared to even go here, due to bad reviews on trip advisor but actually when we got there is was ok, thanks to the advice of previous posts. Firstly as soon as you get on the road towards Mua Cave there will be local people trying to stop you to pay for parking. DO NOT STOP. This is a scam and the people are very forceful just keep riding and say “no thank you”.  They will look offical with signs and whistles. Keep going past. You will know when you get to the end of the road there is a big archway go thru it and there’s the ticket office on the left. DO NOT STOP NEAR THE GATE, there’s also a man there blowing a whistle, just ride past him. This will take a little more stern no if you are on a bicycle.Now your in past the archway and the parking is free. Pay at the ticket counter $100,000VND per person and get walking. They say 500 steps to the top it feels like more ... but will only take about 20 mins depending how much you stop. The view from the top is INCREDIBLE If you can looks past the unfortunate amount of rubbish that has been left behind by other tourists. Please don’t litter this beautiful spot, there are plenty of bins around.We spent about a hour and a half enjoying the view and there is a second peak you can go to as well! A very worth while thing to do in Vietnam, I just hope you read this post first and don’t get scammed along the way :) Happy travels

reviews.author: Paula GE
reviews.title: Totally worth the hike
reviews.content: Great view! Totally worth the hike! Good place to enjoy a beer and the amazing view! Instagramable!!!

reviews.author: an hoang
reviews.title: Not thing
reviews.content: Price for ticket expensive and not thing there. Only see the view. If you are old dont choose this place. And so so so dirty the way go inside. Ticket pay alot of money but why dont make road go inside? So bad. So not recommend this place

reviews.author: Little Daisy77
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: Plan to get here early in the morning (5-6AM) when it’s cool to climb up the stairs. There aren’t any wind when we were there and it’s pretty hot and humid.

reviews.author: alister l
reviews.title: Worth it, but...
reviews.content: Had read about the car park rip offs before hand so was aware of them. They stand in the middle of the road blowing their whistles at you. I aimed for the gap between them, one of them even grabbed my arm on the way past. Someone's going to get badly hurt. If I went again, I'd build up more speed and blow the horn while aiming right for them!! The views are well worth it, surprised at how easy it was, about 10 mins to the top. Very crowded, big groups of noisy Americans (ha) but great 360 views.

reviews.author: Factsnotfiction62
reviews.title: Mua peak - stunning views
reviews.content: We climbed the 500 steps up to the pagada, the views of surrounding Ninh Bing were well worth the effort. Lots of great photo opportunities even on a cloudy day.Lots of places to eat and drink before you go up/come down

reviews.author: rob t
reviews.title: Worth the visit, Lost our GoPro camera there May 19th :(
reviews.content: This place is worth checking out. The climb is quite difficult if you are not in the best of shape, mostly because of the weather (it was 40 degrees C when we went). Not a lot of shade on the way up. Do not get scammed by the motorcycle parking areas on the road in, you DO NOT have to pay to park, drive past them and park for free. We were there on May 19th and lost our GoPro 6 camera!! If anyone finds it, feel free to keep it but the SD card has 3 weeks of all of vacation pictures.. Please.. Please.. Send me a message and I will happily let you keep it for the memory card..

reviews.author: Zuzka Trojka
reviews.title: Nice view, lot of people.
reviews.content: Entrance fee 100000 VDN, lot of people. You can ride motorbike till entrance. Local people want to stop you - quite agressive because of parking.

reviews.author: Kramer
reviews.title: Nice and refreshing Very Place
reviews.content: In order to get to the viewpoint in which you have to climb a good deal of actions, though it's entirely well worthwhile. The suggestions from the most effective are astounding. The Mua Cave in is beautiful. The area below the stairs on the point of view is excellent with small lakes, statues, and plant life.

reviews.author: Jhoice
reviews.title: Stunning panoramic view of the countryside and Ngo Dong River.
reviews.content: I highly recommend going to Mua Caves. You can easily spend 2-3 hours here. The view at the top of the mountain was nothing short of breathtaking. Although trekking up was quite challenging but once you reach the top you will be rewarded with a picturesque view of Ngo Dong River whilst feeling a sense of accomplishment. Definitely put Mua Cave in your itineary if you are visiting Ninh Binh Province.

reviews.author: Adrian Lee
reviews.title: Mr. Adrian Lee
reviews.content: Finally Arrived To The Top Of Mua Caves after climbing more than 950 over steps both ways to enjoy the beautiful panoramic view of Ngo Dong River. 💪🏻💪🏻💪🏻

reviews.author: Stacey M
reviews.title: Worth the steps!
reviews.content: Came here hoping for a good sunset but once up there it didn’t seem like the best spot. Great views up there of all the rice paddies and cliffs. We found a lovely sunset spot just outside the complex, on the left as you leave... there are rice fields you can walk into to get some nice shots of the sun going down! Can confirm with the parking scam, just keep driving down until the end, don’t stop for anyone and the parking is next to the ticket office. Don’t believe the main just outside the gate. Spread the word and let’s stop these locals thinking they can intimidate and scam us tourists :/

reviews.author: Nguyễn Việt Dũng
reviews.title: Cave in Vietnamese means bitch lol
reviews.content: Come here soonest as you can if you dont wanna get burn in here.- Amazing place with many limestone cliffs, me and my friend  started here at 7:45am and it was still hot as hell. You can visit this place in the late afternoon (after 5pm), the weather would be way better.- One more thing, there is a cave under the cliff (i dont remember exactly which one), its the dead end.- I was very disappointed as too many trash here, PLEASE USE YOUR BRAINS TO THROW WASTE IN THE BIN.

reviews.author: Emily G
reviews.title: WARNING: PARKING SCAM
reviews.content: About 500 m from the entrance a woman will blow a whistle and tell you you have to stop (see photo). She is aggressive. KEEP GOING! There is bike and moto parking right next to the entrance & another review even mentioned free parking inside (I can’t verify this). The views are amazing & worth the climb. You can buy drinks, snacks & ice cream about halfway up.

reviews.author: Onie T
reviews.title: Beatiful View at the Top
reviews.content: Visitors must climb around 500 steps to reach the top. In the middle of the climb, the path forks into 2. I chose the left side since our guide said it offers the a more scenic view at the top, though it requires more climbing compared to the right path.The view at the top shows 360 degrees of beautiful Ninh Binh countryside landscape. You can see more limestone mountains up until the horizon, then the river and rice fields below.  You can also see the city from afar.

reviews.author: traveljunkiecris
reviews.title: Worth every step
reviews.content: The view from the top of the cliff is probably one of the best vistas I have ever come across. It's about 500 steps to the top - which get more and more difficult as you ascend, but it is definitely worth the visit. The view of the valley and the cliffs are absolutely amazing. There's about 3 different viewpoints to see once you are up there. All are worth seeing. Do not miss when in Ninh Binh!

reviews.author: Kelly M
reviews.title: Quite nice view but bit of a tourist trap
reviews.content: First of all dont let the crazy agressive people stop you to park there. You can drive all the way through the gate and pay 10.000 to park. The whole thing is a bit of a tourist trap and definitely not worth 100.000. After driving through Ha Giang and seeing amazing mountains we were not too impressed. Also we really notice a huge difference in people.. we feel like a lot of people are trying to rip us off. Not a big fan of Ninh Binh. Would highly recommend renting a motorbike and driving through Ha Giang in stead!!!

reviews.author: SmoothieBighams
reviews.title: Great views, parking is no longer free
reviews.content: Be aware of the other posts regarding the parking touts, dodge them and keep peddling straight down the road, there is offical parking round the back of the ticket booth at the end.  Be aware that it is no longer free, it is 5k for a bike, 10k for a scooter and 20k for a car.  There is a sign with the parking prices on the side window of the ticket booth if you are uncertain.  It is 100k entry pp.  Enjoy the great views!

reviews.author: Varun_723
reviews.title: Tiring but worth it
reviews.content: Mua Cave and Mua Peak are both located at the same spot, and offer some of the best views in Ninh Binh. While the walk to the top can be tiring, it's worth it. The entrance ticket costs 100,000 dong per person, don't worry if you don't have cash, they accept all major credit cards. When you go up the stairs you'll eventually reach a fork with staircases headed in different directions. The one of the right goes to a small shrine, while the one on the left goes to the dragon peak which is higher up. Unless you want to go to both viewpoints, my advice would be to take the stairs on the left to the dragon peak, it's higher up and has a better view of the area. Dragon Peak also gives you a great view of the river behind it where you can see people on their boat rides through the limestone karsts.When it comes to taking a photograph at the top, exercise as much caution as possible. As you can probably imagine, there's absolutely no safety barriers or protection. Some people like to climb onto the shrine, or stand by the side of the stone dragon for photographs, both of which are very precariously perched. The rock surface surrounding the dragon in particular is very jagged and offers little stability. There are much safer spots for photographs but if you choose to risk it, go slow and be aware of the sheer drop on the other side. It's also best to wear sports shoes if you're visiting during or immediately after rain cause the stairs can get very slippery.

reviews.author: KathrynandDavid
reviews.title: Cool view
reviews.content: Cool views, millions of stairs up a steep ascent- still only took 20mins. Plenty of spots to take pics on the way to the stairs and once you start climbing. Free toilets closer to the beginning of the stairs. Parking 10k for motobikes, beware of crazy ladies jumping out in front of your bike to make you come to theirs. Get as close to the ticket booth as possible. Still pay probably but less to walk. Sad to see so much rubbish everywhere and part of the walk was closed off for what looked like a photo shoot.

reviews.author: Jessica A
reviews.title: Avoid the "parking mafia" and drive past the Eco Lodge gates
reviews.content: As many previous reviewers have suggested, don't get conned into parking outside the Caves entrance. The entrance is actually within the Eco Lodge - once you get past the gates you can buy your entrance tickets and then keep driving to the parking. You walk through the Eco Lodge to get to the cave and viewpoint. You can go through the cave if you'd like (very quick trip) to a nice little field on the other side, then the steps up to the viewpoints are after the cave. The steps are quite steep and you will get very sweaty! It isn't a long walk though - I think it took us less than half an hour up and down, though we only went to one viewpoint. I recommend going to the dragon viewpoint first as this is higher - you can see the second viewpoint from there and decide if it's worth going to. To me it looked like the view wouldn't be any different, so we just headed down.The views are amazing and well worth the walk.Our accommodation told us that they stop selling tickets at 5pm (but the attraction is open beyond that), so check that if you're planning on going there in the late afternoon.

reviews.author: PatXN
reviews.title: Awful place
reviews.content: The view from the top is nice, but I don’t think it’s worth the price. Also, the parking scam is very irritating, lots of people aggressively trying to stop you on the way to the entrance. We managed to avoid being stopped but finally the lady selling tickets told us we have to park outside because there is no free parking. This of course turned out to be a lie, which is ridiculous. I don’t mind paying for the parking, but I don’t like to be trick into doing it. There are much nicer places to visit in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Hannah Proud
reviews.title: Don't let the steps put you off!
reviews.content: Incredible views from the top, definitely worth all the steep steps and tourists! Honestly one of the most beautiful views, was completely blown away.

reviews.author: Lavender
reviews.title: Crowded place but nice area
reviews.content: At the entrace you have to pay fee for parking bike and bicycle. We pass the entrance, paid 100kVND and climbed up to top of mountain. Place was so crowded, I was pushed many times by people running to take picture in famous pagoda. Terrain was not stable, lot of cobblestones, mosquitos and people of course. Place itself is really nice, it is worth to see.

reviews.author: Sarah
reviews.title: Well worth the climb...beware of parking scam
reviews.content: The view at the top is well worth the climb. I recommend leaving Tam Coc/Ninh Binh at 6am to beat the heat as the climb is steep. Beware of the ‘parking mafia’ don’t stop driving until you reach the end of the road. Drive past the ticket station and park your scooter in the offical car park (cost 10,000 for parking there) and pay the 100,000 dong fee for the viewpoint. Locals will be standing on the road in Vietcong hats and with whistles trying to stop you and make you park in their park and pay more for parking. They will try to stand into front of your scooter yelling at you and blocking your way...JUST KEEP GOING...DON’T STOP!

reviews.author: Big Asian Choice
reviews.title: Masterpiece Blend of Nature and Culture
reviews.content: Mua Caves is part of the Trang An Landscape Complex (UNESCO World Heritage since 2014) and Mua Hill is one of the best viewpoints to view part of this landscape complex. The limestone of Mua Hill is curiously and beautifully black or near black in colour. The steps up to Mua Hill bring you to at least 5 lookouts, to view Tam Coc area and padi field plain. There are also pagoda structures seen here. These man made features blend effortlessly with the nature surrounding, providing a feeling of peace and harmony, which made this landscape unique from many other karst landscapes found across Asia and the World.

reviews.author: chutotoro
reviews.title: Good exercise, excellent views
reviews.content: About 500 steps to the top, a very workout. Staircases can be steep, be sure to wear good hiking shoes. The views on top was stunning. On one side you can see Tam Coc, another side the paddy field and roads.

reviews.author: david and leann... c
reviews.title: great even on a busy day
reviews.content: get in early of late if you are visiting on a public holiday.worth spending some time on the two tops to see the views.

reviews.author: Don C
reviews.title: Another Climb - Whew
reviews.content: The climb to the top (500 steps) is worth it.  If you are seasoned like we are you just need to pace yourself.  Since the steps are uneven Trekking Poles help.  The grounds are also quite nice, just lots of trash.

reviews.author: suzieslapcabbage
reviews.title: Stunning view
reviews.content: Well worth the early rise to head up the 500 steps to view the valley. We entered about 7.15am and basically had the climb and view to ourselves. It may seem a lot of steps but we paced ourselves and the view is more than worth the effort, it is absolutely stunning and one of our favourite memories from our trip to Vietnam.

reviews.author: Andreas M
reviews.title: Shameful locals but still a not to miss place.
reviews.content: Ok. The place is really great from a visual perspective. There is the actual Hung Mua cave to explore, that opens up into a mountain-ringed-valley that visitors seem to skip. (They tend) to only for for the 500+ steps to the top of one of the two peaks.)We went toward the late afternoon when it is peak time for visitors. But the number of visitors didn’t bother us as everyone was courteous and fairly quiet to take in the breathtaking views. We also took lots of amazing pics in the cave area and from the top of one of the two peaks. However, and this is where it “sucks” and only gets 3* instead of 5*, mins the following:1. Local parking mafia (Parking Scan)As you approach, there will be restaurants along the road, asking you or offering you to park your bike there. Don’t pay them any mind, they won’t bother you, just keep on driving to get closer to the main entrance gate. Here is where it gets hairy and tricky. It will be chaotic. So will see a few people trying to direct you with whistle and hand gestures to a parking lot across from the gate on the OUTSIDE of the complex. Do not listen to them nor follow their directions. Politely say no, you will park inside. They cannot force you. Instead, proceed slowly in a non-threatening manner toward the gate, enter the inner complex and you will see on your immediate left the ticketing office and right behind there on the left is the scooter parking. Park your bike there. There will be a guy with a Viet-Kong style hat, who will ask you for money. This is OK. They recently, officially, started charging for motor cycle parking, 10,000 Vietnamese dong. Bicycles are 5000 Vietnamese dong. However, if he does ask you to park outside the gate, don’t do it, because he is in cahoots with the local Vietnamese parking mafia as I called them, who will charge you 15,000 Vietnamese dong & more to park your bike outside the gates.Once you have parked your motorcycle/scooter/bicycle, go to the ticketing office, pay your 100,000 down entrance fee and proceed on into the complex.2. Aggressive localsThere is a young Vietnamese guy, probably in his early 20s, who is part of the parking mafia. We saw him very aggressive towards tourists and other visitors alike, trying to scam them for money or try to get a Vietnamese guide to pay for his western clients more than what they should be paying for no service or anything tangible. They even went as far as driving fast after a western European guy and his Vietnamese guide/girlfriend. They finally caught up with them 500 meters down the road and were threatening both while yelling in Vietnamese. Since my partner is Vietnamese, he was able to understand what the your vier mafia guy was yelling. And it is exactly as I described above. The young guy tried to extort money out of the Vietnamese woman, paying for the western guy extra money that was not needed nor a required or warranted.So at the end of the day, if you steer clear of the parking mafia and you don’t mind it being a little bit crowded, it is well worth the visit. Do not miss the cave, once you are inside the complex, it will be on the left side after some Bungalo‘s, just follow the half circle going left. I do not believe that you should boycott this attraction just because of local idiots.Also, the young, aggressive Vietnamese parking mafia guy seems to be the same one as mentioned in another review a few weeks ago. I just wish that the police would actually stand there instead of tolerating this kind of behavior. But police is nowhere to be found in this town - AT ALL. Shame on the police and shame on some of the locals who are acting in a total shameful manner.

reviews.author: Leo K
reviews.title: Scammers, Tourist trap, Fake-otourist lodge,...
reviews.content: Firstly you have to avoid the scammers for parking that are aggressive and order you to stop. Say no politely and go on even if they insist. They have no right to stop you.Secondly, my girlfriend and I just wanted to climb to the top to enjoy the view. We thought we could go by ourselves along the small path near the huge "Eco"lodge. We then realized that we had to go through this fake and plastic-made place to climb the mountain. Nothing is authentic, it is all constructed to attract tourists and get more money.We went back and decided not to go because this is too fake and the scammers ruin our motivation.If you are a real tourist looking for authenticity, do them a favor and do not go there. Maybe they will then change their behavior and their approach of tourism.

reviews.author: Ellen B
reviews.title: Steep climb but worth it
reviews.content: Bring plenty of water and take your time Very touristic, as always there are heaps of Vietnamese people taking lots of photos in different positions, but the photos in the end of the Tam Coc area are worth it. Almost 500 steps.

reviews.author: Tony B
reviews.title: Mau Caves
reviews.content: This is a must do if you come to Ninh Binh or Tam Coc. The walk up the 800 steps are worth it. The views from the top are spectacular. One of the highlights of our trip to the area.

reviews.author: rz7692
reviews.title: Good views even on cloudy day
reviews.content: Once again the other reviewers are correct about parking scams. One lady jumped in front of my motor bike and I almost ran her over just because she wanted me to park. When I tried to park for free at the entrance a guy told me I must pay and when I said no he started wheeling my motorbike away so I paid 10000. Otherwise we enjoyed the views from the top very much. The climb only took about 20-25 minutes. I didn’t even do it very fast but 500 steps goes quick. Beware of the parking but otherwise I recommend it!

reviews.author: Lyonng
reviews.title: Nice view from top
reviews.content: Visited Mua Cave as part of the day trip to Ninh Binh.  The tour guide said it was 496 steps to be exact, though most tour introduction mentioned 500 steps up.Not an easy climb for me (who is in the mid 50s) and finally made it through the top in about 30 mins or so.  The weather was not at its best but we were lucky the rain stopped when we got there as it was drizzling most of the morning.There were 2 peaks at the top.  We took the left path that leads us to the peak overseeing the Tam Coc river.  We could see tiny bamboo boats moving in the river very much like small little toys.  We could also view the peak at the opposite end overseeing the green rice fields.Time and energy level didn't allow us to climb the other peak. Going down the steps is another challenge but definitely much more easier than climbing up.Overall a great experience.  Don't miss it if you visit Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Jmchan91
reviews.title: Rubbish dump
reviews.content: TOURIST TRAP. I would give it 0 stars. You can do a nicer walk for free else where. It is appalling that they charge 100k for a few flight of stairs. The view is OK, if you have been to real national parks in China or other places this is absolutely not worth it. We came at 5:30sm and bought our tickets. Inside, there is RUBBISH EVERYWHERE. When you reach the dragon at the top, you realise they also use that as a tipping ground for trash. Where does the entry fee go towards since there is clearly no maintenance here. It made me feel sick to see how they treat the land and then overcharge for it. DO NOT SUPPORT THEM.

reviews.author: LondonFoodLover909
reviews.title: Parking scam turned violent
reviews.content: We parked our motorbikes in the free area next to the ticket booth. Some men approached and told us to pay 10,000 however we knew it was free parking included in the price. When we returned our bikes had gone. We finally found them in a different parking area around the corner. One guy came up to us and demanded money, when we said no and asked why he’d moved our bikes he became furious, ran off and grabbed a large brick which he ran up to my friend with waving it in his face threatening to hit him. The situation was extremely aggressive and scary and to avoid serious violence I paid the man and he gave me back my key which he’d stolen from my ignition. We drove off extremely distressed and as we left the same guy threw bricks at us, aiming to hit not just to scare. Luckily his aim was bad. Hopefully someone working in the cave tourist industry reads this and does something to stop this crime.

reviews.author: Janie
reviews.title: Aggressive “parking attendants”
reviews.content: The viewpoint itself is totally worth the climb of the very steep steps! Beautiful views!However, we had our experience tainted as on the way in (on the road leading to the attraction) we were accosted by aggressive locals trying to get you into their parking areas - this is a scam. One young man stood in front of our bike and wouldn’t move until we told him that we already came the day before and know the parking is free. If you manage to carry on right through the entry gates parking is FREE. We still ended up paying a smaller amount at the end as we thought that was official until we walked through the gates. All the parked motorbikes are hidden around the corner so that people park in the areas leading up to the actual attraction.

reviews.author: hfffoman
reviews.title: Pleasant climb
reviews.content: Worth the climb but not a must-see. The caves are not worth seeing.  Hire bikes and cycle there across the fields. It's a wonderful area.

reviews.author: alohabic
reviews.title: stunning view
reviews.content: it is quite a climb to get to the top but definitely worth it, the views are stunning on both places

reviews.author: Harry
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: One of the most beautyfull place in Ninh Binh. One night is not enough, will be back and stay longer

reviews.author: Max Rombouts
reviews.title: Great view but be aware of the scams
reviews.content: The view point is really great. On one side you can see ninh binh and on the other side parts of tam coc.But be wary of the scams when traveling with motor or bicycle. Before the ticket both they will try to let you park either with intimidation or threatening you. Stand your ground park inside the walls of the ticket booth buy a ticket and parking is free. Wenn they yell at you or want to force you by grabbing you give them a taste of their own medicine. Yell curses at them in your native language, stare really angry at them in the eyes and give them a push if need be. They get scared and run off. The scammers are like 40 kilos so even small women would be stronger than they are any day of the week. And spread the word of this scam to fellow travellers wenn they arrive. Just to piss of the scammers more.

reviews.author: iulianito
reviews.title: Beware: parking scam!!!!
reviews.content: Fabulous siteBUTbe aware that you dont have to park before the site and payYour ticket gives you access to a parking

reviews.author: Immanuel R
reviews.title: Great views of the valley!
reviews.content: The views are amazing! You can a get of the river in Tam Coc that had the Samoan boat tour. If you're already in the area, worth a visit, especially good photo opportunities during sunset. However, you'll need to climb around 500 steps up and the steps are quite steep towards the top. You'll be rewarded with an amazing views though. Naturally, this is not suitable for those who are not in the best of shape but you can take your time climbing the stairs. Be careful going down as well.

reviews.author: AnniK0210
reviews.title: Great place but very busy
reviews.content: Firstly don't let the people at the 'parking' places fool you. There's parking at the entrance.Hang mua itself is great (although it looks like they are just trying to turn it into a park on the bottom ). It was very busy but definitely worth it.

reviews.author: Lya_amar
reviews.title: Gem of Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Worth the 500 step climb to the top. The view was majestic and stunning. Go early in the morning to avoid crowd or in the evening to watch sunset. :)

reviews.author: Jaclynornai
reviews.title: Great activity
reviews.content: Nice walk up the stairs and beautiful view from the top! There are restaurants at the bottom which is really nice to stop for a beer and an ice cream after! Definitely glad we did this!

reviews.author: smt000
reviews.title: Great view, bad service
reviews.content: The walk is worth it with amazing and beautiful views over the valley. The first thing though are the rude people that try and get you to park at their shop and ask for money for parking. They just straight out lie to you that you have to walk the last part. The second is the rude people that work inside. They act like you are bothering them if you want a drink or anything for that matter. Third, clean up the bits of rubbish at the top Vietnamese people, stop just counting the money and do something to preserve this beautiful place.

reviews.author: Anne
reviews.title: PARKING SCAMS: THERE'S A FREE PARKING NEAR THE TICKET BOOTH (scooter and bicycle)
reviews.content: Do not be fooled by the four or five women who whistle you when you approach the entrance of Mua caves : they will want you to pay a huge amount of money to park (normally 5000 dongs in Vietnam for a scooter, here is 15 to 50k dongs). Avoid them (they will try to block the way and lie to you, saying that you cannot go further), also avoid the last parking just next to the parking for cars and go STRAIGHT to the ticket booth (be brave).Parking is FREE at Mua Caves if you buy an entry ticket (100 000 dongs). Even if you manage to park near the ticket booth on the site itself, a guy may come and ask you for 10 000 dongs (he will give you a receipt). Just ignore him and go straight to the ticket booth to pay for your entry. He'll surely tell something in Vietnamese to the lady at the counter, she'll explain to you that since one month now (what a coincidence), you have to pay 10 000 dongs to park. Just say to her that it's free, pay the entry and enjoy. They won't ask for any money when you come back to leave.As for the viewpoint... we went there before 9 AM and we were lucky. After 9 AM, a lot of locals and tourists were already on their way to the top, making the descent quite hard for us. This is - by far - the worst site (regarding the scams) that we visited around Tam Coc.

reviews.author: 951hanhp
reviews.title: majestic
reviews.content: I am not young but I was very happy when I visited this place. The scene from above is very beautiful and you will have a good photo when shooting here to show off to your friends.

reviews.author: E J J
reviews.title: Top of the World
reviews.content: That's what it feels like when you get to the top. Spectacular views up there. It was a hard climb, for me, but if you take little breaks along the way and admire the views all the way up, you'll make it. It's very busy on the week ends, but if you can visit during the week, it's a lot quieter. Definitely worth it!

reviews.author: JuCoAbroad
reviews.title: Beautiful scenery, worth a trip
reviews.content: Dry Ha long bay is a quite fitting description. Slightly crowded with white people but still enjoyable. Definitely worth a day trip.

reviews.author: Karina P
reviews.title: Mua caves and Tam Coc
reviews.content: Went as a privat tour, because you can not go to these 2 places together as a group.Costed us 160 USD, pic upfrom the old quarter.Very beautiful place.Can be very crowded, I would think again about going her in high season.We were lucky and could sail most of our trip "alone", so it seemed to be a quiet and peaceful place.The trip was included in our tour, but I think it was around 50.000 dong.The boatman expect a tip, 50.000 If okay trip, 100.000 If you are very happy.The trip takes around 1,5 hour, and the boatman pedels all the time, so they deserv a little for their effort.

reviews.author: Stephenie T
reviews.title: Great View Point, but crowded with selfie takers
reviews.content: Came here while visiting Ninh Binh.  The viewpoint cost 100000 dong to visit, and there is no shortage of visitors here.  We happened to come a sunset which wasn't planned but a nice bonus.  There are two view points and both have lots of people waiting around at key spots to take selfies.  Not my thing so it does ruin the mood a bit, but such is travel in the age of instagram.  Still I highly recommend coming here in when visiting Ninh Binh/Tam Coc

reviews.author: optimus07
reviews.title: Beautiful spot view
reviews.content: The place has one of the best spots to see the region from above. Going through a newly created park (restaurants, hotels, etc) you can start climbing the 500 steps. At the beginning it is quite easy but the more you go up the more it becomes steep and harder. Just take it easy and climb it slowly and admire the view through the way up. The entrance is 100k VND and the parking is 10k VND (you can park inside just after buying the entrance tickets so don’t park it outside where a lot of scammers are).We were on a Saturday around noon and there were not lot of people there and the place was not as dirty as I read in the previous comments even if there are some spots not clean. Worth the visit for sure!

reviews.author: planetawdrodze
reviews.title: Wow!
reviews.content: This is one of the best things ive seen in Vietnam! If you are going by motorbike remember that you can park for free just near ticket office and ignore people who are forcing you to park on some parking spots and pay for that.

reviews.author: Sam E
reviews.title: Fabulous view
reviews.content: It's a bit of a climb, but the view is spectacular.
