You can see the rice fields on one side and the river where the tam coc boat tours go through on the other. We went around 11 am and there weren't too many people around. I'd give yourself an hour or two to mess around, get some good photos, rest on your way up and soak in the scenery. You must pay to park your bike and then pay for the entrance but it's worth every penny. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Cathleen D
reviews.title: Incredible - must do in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Highlight of Ninh Binh!! Long climb up but totally worth it - great photo ops and wow what an amazing view. Ticket entry is 100000 VND pp. A must do if you’re in the area!!

reviews.author: inkkie7 .
reviews.title: Fun climb!
reviews.content: I was surprised my 4 yr old daughter enjoyed climbing up & down the hill without complaining of tiredness. Even young men were stopping for breath. It was rather fun & challenging to climb especially for a housewife like me but the view on top was awesome. We even saw couples taking wedding photos on top. Hats off to the bride for climbing up in her pouffy bridal gown! 👰🏻

reviews.author: Mayank Agarwal
reviews.title: Beautiful Views, Awesome Picture opportunity, Hikes Gives Sense of Self Accomplishment
reviews.content: The cave itself is rubbish, you visit for the views from the peak above which require a good hike. If you don’t like hiking/climbing, it’s better to skip the site. The climb of about 500 steps is paved but very steep in the end. Normally people do it in 15 minutes, we ourselves must have taken 30 to 40 minutes (well I am obese).  Felt it’s totally worth it for the amazing unobstructed views of Tom Coc on one side and the rural village view on the other side. It’s advisable to carry a bottle of water as there are no refreshment points on the way up. Entry Fees is 100,000 VND.The climb starts from Mua Caves Ecolodge, a great option for people to stay over as I am sure the views would be more enchanting at sunrise or sunset. There is a cafeteria at the start of the climb beside a pond, got hammocks and a garden style setup.

reviews.author: Sander B
reviews.title: Great view - must go
reviews.content: Great view, must go! There a lot of steps to The top, but The view is very rewarding. All around Great experience.

reviews.author: Ellie200809
reviews.title: 500 steps 👍
reviews.content: You must pass the 500 steps to climb to the top of the mountain . stand from above you can see the panoramic view of the city of Ninh Binh , Ngo Dong River to the small boat into Tam COC .This is an attractive destination you should not miss.You should go to the rice harvest season in Ninh Binh to watch the scenery of rice fields.

reviews.author: richmond144
reviews.title: Not a cave at all--but better!
reviews.content: Mua Caves is not a cave. It's a collection of karsts (the mountainous landforms you see in the pictures). A visit to Mua Caves involves a rather steep hike up stone steps where you will be rewarded with refreshing breezes and amazing views overlooking the karsts, rice paddies, and Ninh Binh. Don't miss this scenic trek!At the bottom of the hike, there are two large swings overlooking the rice fields and a short fairly level path that walks around a pond. If some members of your party aren't up for the climb, there is a lovely area for them to enjoy near the bottom.

reviews.author: Utterchaos
reviews.title: Ordinary caves
reviews.content: The caves are really nothing to see, but the climb up the Lying Dragon path is worthwhile for the view. This is included if you are staying at the Ecolodge. Be aware that if you are older or you are carrying an injury that parts of the steps are quite uneven and could present a challenge. There are quite a few places to stop and rest on the way up. Recommend first thing in the morning or late afternoon for this activity.

reviews.author: Ashton Tessier
reviews.title: More like Mua Hike...
reviews.content: Not sure why the spot is called Mua Caves. The caves were a disappointment, especially after they charge 100,000 dong per person to enter, however there is a spectacular view after a little bit of a climb up the mountain. The view from the top was gorgeous. I wouldn't put this at the top of my must do's, but it was still nice to see!!

reviews.author: tlord2017
reviews.title: Well worth the climb
reviews.content: How often do you go somewhere on a staff recommendation only to meet people who have come to this one place as an item on their bucket list. The trip up and down (the steps are SERIOUS climbing) was great and the chats with people from around the world was fun. strenuous but fun.

reviews.author: TravelWanderlust90
reviews.title: A high high steps to reach the Lying Dragon!!
reviews.content: Travelled with my friends to Mua Caves, I have no idea to go in Trang An but followed my friends. *Mua Cave is not a CAVE* which I dont know why they call it a CAVE???!Instead is a-at-least 5-600 step stair to the top. OK, you are able to observe the spectacular peaceful view of Trang An, but the steps are tighter and steeper when you nearly reach the top peak without any handrail which is terrified.Another point : they charge 100,000 VND for entrance fee that is ridiculously high compares to Vietnam living expenses. All of my friends complained about it.For those who are afraid of the height - this is not an ideal place!!!

reviews.author: hayleyniad
reviews.title: Nice views
reviews.content: We came expecting to see a cave, which may have been our fault for not reading the reviews first.  The views from the top were very pretty but if you are doing other climbing activities in the area you’re likely to see similar views.  Also, I applaud those reviewers who have called this an easy 15 minute hike - I am in reasonably good shape and found this to be a very challenging number of steep steps to handle!

reviews.author: kyy0te
reviews.title: Not the caves, but the steps to the Lying Dragon
reviews.content: The caves were unimpressive unless we missed something, but climbing the steps up the mountain was definitely worth it.

reviews.author: Jesse F
reviews.title: Excellent views one hell of a walk
reviews.content: Apparently this is about 500 steps upwards and im still feeling every one of them, but the view was worth it. Great photo opportunities on the way back.

reviews.author: BillyGre
reviews.title: Great view
reviews.content: We paid 10$ for tickets and spent around 1 hour to visit the cave. It took 15 minutes to climb up and we saw wonderful view from the top. However, the cave was quite small and not special like caves in Halong Bay. In general, a must see in Ninh Binh!

reviews.author: Sofía GG :)
reviews.title: BREATHTAKING
reviews.content: Definitely worth it! My favourite attraction in North Vietnam. The scenery is just amazing. I recommend going in the afternoon and staying at the top to see the sunset!!

reviews.author: Sancho D
reviews.title: Beautiful 360 view on top
reviews.content: Easy to get there biking from Tam Coc center (8 km), 100k for a ticket + 5k for each bike you park. Pretty site from entry up to the steps, and once you climbed all of the 450 steps (not too hard, just do as many stops as you need), really nice view with rice fields and Ninh Bing plain on one side, river and Vietnamese typical rocks on the other side.

reviews.author: Rachel B
reviews.title: Mua cave - a must see! Great view point!
reviews.content: Regular tourist tours from Hanoi don’t come to this look out pint but it is worth the trip. 580 stairs and you will find a great view around you... We took a private tour of the area just to get here. Don’t miss it

reviews.author: HWKhor
reviews.title: Short hike with a scenic view
reviews.content: It's a short hike up the cave and along the way you can catch great views! Recommended activity. Fresh air and nice top view looking down from the top of the cave.

reviews.author: Damian J
reviews.title: Incredible view
reviews.content: We went there at the morning and it was uncrowded and quiet. There are many parkings outside the lodge. It's a quite requirement to get to the top especially in hot and high humidity. Additional impediment is that steps are different heigh and some of them are really high. It definitely worth climbing the stairs to see view from the top.

reviews.author: cecillie m
reviews.title: beautiful view!
reviews.content: A short climb to a beautiful view of Ninh Binh! We stayed in Mua Cave Ecolodge so our climb here is free. They said it looked best before harvest time. But it still look amazing when we gt there. They open at 7am-5pm

reviews.author: TerryTeo
reviews.title: My highlight in Ninh Binh!
reviews.content: I came here and hiked up around 4pm. There were considerable of crowd as everyone was trying to catch the spectacular sunset over the Tam Coc rice field from the top. The hike up took around 20 minutes. The flight of stairs could be challenging but not impossible. The sunset view was mind-blowing and please get the sunset timing right when you visit. I saw 2 men started the ascend when everyone was descending and I would have thought they missed the sunset, unless they were staying there for couple of days. Please be vigilant of the safety around this area - as I personally think this area would not meet many international safety standards for visit. There were no proper signage, railing and fencing at the top. Just be extra cautious.

reviews.author: Rico
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: The clime is worth is and gives you a really nice view of the city. Not sure about the cave there was water in there and could no go in there. The clime to the top was around 25 - 30 minutes for me. The price is 100.000 for a adult which is a little high for what you get I think.

reviews.author: Wayne B
reviews.title: Great view
reviews.content: We didn't bother going to Mua Cave as we really wanted to climb to the top of Mua Hill.The stairs are a bit uneven but the effort of climbing the 450 steps is worthwhile.Even though the day we went was overcast we still had a great view of the surrounding countryside.There are several places where you can stop and rest and take photos.

reviews.author: Titran
reviews.title: A must see in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: It is worth climbing 500 steps to be on the top. The whole Tam Coc landscape is revealed and this should be a must visit apart from Tam Coc and Trang An boat tours.

reviews.author: ndglamr
reviews.title: Great view!
reviews.content: This is a hidden gem! The climb to the top was fantastic and not impossible. My wife and I did it with our daughter (two years old). You get a fantastic view of the area, and on the ground it is a great place to walk a round and just get a break from busy tourist attractions.

reviews.author: Valentina F
reviews.title: Challenging hike up to Mua Caves
reviews.content: This cave complex was my favorite part of our Vietnam trek - easily the best views. The hike up to the top of the cave complex was extremely welcome after several days of lazing around on our Ha Long Bay cruise. I’ll let the photos speak for themselves!

reviews.author: Ondřej K
reviews.title: Price is bit inadequate
reviews.content: The cave is not really the reason to go there. The view is not bad (probably depends on season) but after visiting north of Vietnam nothing special. 100.000 VND for entrance is ok if it’s the only peak you visit in Vietnam, otherwise i would think twice whether to go there.

reviews.author: lidkaa
reviews.title: Very nice place but be careful...
reviews.content: ... if you go there by motorbike or bike. There are people that will try to stop you on the way there to leave bike/motorbike on their parking for 5K. There is a free parking lot behind the gate.The caves are nothing special but the view from the top of the Lying Dragon Mountain is really nice :)

reviews.author: BVL69
reviews.title: We climbed to the temples above Mua Cave ; the view was stunning, even on a cloudy misty day.
reviews.content: The cave was small and not very interesting. However the climb to the temples above the cave was really worthwhile with stunning views over to Ninh Binh and on the other side over the river system that boats row along. We did a boat trip the next day from Trang An; we thoroughly enjoyed it even in light rain - we passed through low caves and stopped at a temple.

reviews.author: James L
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: Go for the sunset view. The panoramic view of the landscape and river below was breathtaking. It’s totally worth the 100k price of entry and the nearly 500 steps up. It’s not that difficult. We saw young children at the peak.

reviews.author: JunJie4
reviews.title: Really cool view from the top
reviews.content: The view up above is just amazing. After the 500 steps, if you're feeling adventurous, please do climb up to the dragon. I waited for the sunset on the dragon and it was beautiful.

reviews.title: Amazing views!
reviews.content: A long long walk up many steps but the views are absolutely worth the struggle! 100,000 vnd entry fee. Roughly £4, worth every penny. Area is clean and plenty of parking space for scooters and motorbikes.

reviews.author: MarSca
reviews.title: Nice view from up there
reviews.content: The stairs are very steep. A decent physical condition is recommended, cause the steps can be as high as 40/50 cm. It took us 45 minutes up and down with numerous breaks for pictures.The view from up there is really nice

reviews.author: Emma W
reviews.title: Excellent views but expensive
reviews.content: Having cycled to Trang An we stopped at Mua Caves on our way back to the homestay. We climbed the hill to the dragon and the views were amazing. But for the entry fee this was an expensive view as the cave was not worth the visit.

reviews.author: Nhi H
reviews.title: Very nice view
reviews.content: After climbing a lot of stairs and being exhausted, you will enjoy a very nice view from above of Mua Cave Not bad for spending time

reviews.author: Thomas v
reviews.title: Mua "cave" / staircase +view
reviews.content: The cave is not worth mentioning. instead you should just do the stairs that start at the "cave". Once you reach the top you'll get a terrific view on the rice fields and surrounding area. (at most touristic stops there will be parking incl "security" which will ask a small fee for "securing" your bike or scooter... Don't know if they are legit so sometimes we paid them, sometimes we didn't...)

reviews.author: emilita13
reviews.title: Trip with Indochina Junk
reviews.content: We took a day trip from Hanoi to Ninh Binh with Indochina Junk.  They picked us up from our hotel and drove us back at the end of the day. We had bikes ready and waiting with our guide.  We biked around 30kms and hiked up Mua Cave. It was spectacular!! It's not busy or touristy -- and the view is worth the climb up.

reviews.author: Luca C
reviews.title: Every effort's repaid
reviews.content: 500 steps under the burning Vietnamese Sun could be very hard to face for someone.Actually, it's not easy as a walk on the beach during the spring season, but I swear that the view on the top repays from every effort.I absolutely suggest not to miss it ( and to spend at least 2 days in the wonderful Ninh Binh )

reviews.author: Minh Châu P
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: Should go in April since it offers the view of the golden rice field. Otherwise weather in Oct is really comfortable for travelling

reviews.author: Sonnycolin
reviews.title: Awesome viewpoint
reviews.content: Hike for about 10 min to the top. My gf found the high steps pretty challenging but doable. The view is amazing. Tip: If you are up for it, go climb a bit onto the rocks, Some pretty cool photo spots are there to be found.

reviews.author: Yannis L
reviews.title: Must come!
reviews.content: The entrance fee is 100,00 Đồng. To get to the TOP you have to climb 500 steps up the hill. But once u are up there, the view is totally worth it! Not only u get to see the city view, u also get to see the stunning nature landscape. Highly recommended to anyone who wish to see the landscapes

reviews.author: cannga1
reviews.title: Stunning - Ninh Binh is not complete without this view from top. ;-)
reviews.content: Although Mua Cave is at ground level, as part of the visit you would climb to the mountain top right above Mua Cave (a short climb on stairs). From here, you get a rare and spectacular view of the limestone mountains and river from ABOVE (as opposed to view from the boat). The view from top gives a much better appreciation of the stunning beauty of the area IMHO.Especially if you are into photography, make sure to add Mua Cave to the itinerary.

reviews.author: Elmer S
reviews.title: Tripled the entry price!
reviews.content: Great view from the top (after a long climb, try to do this in the early morning or late afternoon) but the entry fee is way too high. They more than tripled it compared to our 2016 Lonely Planet: from 30k to 100k dong per person.  Parking is free though, skip the hawkers in front of the entrance, there's a parking spot for your (motor) bike just beyond the gate.

reviews.author: mena s
reviews.title: Amazing View
reviews.content: Unfortunately the caves were flooded and we had to take a boat to get to the entrace. But the scenery is just breathteaking

reviews.author: Daan A
reviews.title: Have you ever seen the rain?
reviews.content: Caves were flooded when we got there. However, climbing the chairs in the torrential rain storm during a tropical storm while the road were flooded was truly epic. Bucketlist. Authentic. Propper millenial stuff ;-).

reviews.author: Hang Ng
reviews.title: Stunning sunset!
reviews.content: It might be a bit slippery climbing up, so get ready with a proper shoes. The view will worth your effort! they said ticket is a bit pricey but let's forget it. The view will worth you more than it

reviews.author: Kevin O
reviews.title: Epic views
reviews.content: This is a must see, King Kong filmed here, you sort of feel when your at the top, he is going to jump out at you.

reviews.author: David O
reviews.title: Panoramic view of Tam Coc
reviews.content: I rented a local bicycle and find my way through the local village, grave yards, rice fields, mud tracks and finally arrived at Hang Mua.Entrance fee is 100,000.00 Dong. Walk right in passing the eco-lodges along the stone footpath and up a constructed stone stair case up Hang Mua.Once reaching the top , the view is fabulous, overlooking the rice fields below and the river on the other.

reviews.author: Risha D
reviews.content: if there's one thing you are planning on doing in Tam Coc, let it be this one. you'll leave speechless! make sure you have a lot of water beforehand. :)

reviews.author: Chua K
reviews.title: Early morning or late afternoon visit will be good, a good 1 hour climb
reviews.content: Hugely popular with day trippers, combining Mua Cave with Hoa Lu temple and the boat ride.  Avoid weekends. Scenic view at the top, looking over the limestone karst hills and rivers. We cycled here from Tam Coc town, a pleasant morning cycle. Verdict: just ok for 100,000 VND entry fee. Guilin in China views are more dramatic.

reviews.author: Paul M
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: A nice bike ride from Tam Coc town centre. On arrival we looked for somewhere to park our bikes. Don't be fooled by the guy who tells you to park in front of his shop, he'll expect you to pay and we found out afterwards that we could have parked in an area where we bought a ticket! After you get your ticket you follow the path towards the caves. There are a few caves here, one will lead to a café where you can get yourself a cold drink before or after you climb. Another small cave is full of ankle deep water which leads to  a dead end, this cave is at the bottom of the stairs you'll climb to the top.The stair climb is pretty moderate, we climbed at 1200 so it was stupid hot and we found It a struggle. As you climb you will begin to see amazing views. They get better as you climb higher and higher so I'd recommend just getting to the top before you start taking you pictures. There are two peaks here, which we were not aware of. They are both worth climbing.

reviews.author: Kaylee05
reviews.title: Breath-taking sunset
reviews.content: We stay near Tam Coc and then take a bicycle to Hang Mua. It's so peaceful and beautiful along the way to Hang Mua. You can witness the local farmer working in the rice fields.  I think the best time to go Hang Mua is afternoon, you climb to the top and admire the golden rice fields and catch the scarce moment of the sunset here.

reviews.author: andrew-jerusalem
reviews.title: Nice view but was it worth the climb?
reviews.content: We cycled to the mua cave from tam coc which is about 7 km and the ride itself was nice. The cave is nothing special, what you really go for is the view from the top of the hill. But 300 plus steps in 32c heat and 100% humidity is not fun. Would only recommend if you are coming in a cooler part of the year

reviews.author: HongvanLe1
reviews.title: Great View to the field
reviews.content: Better go the in the after noon. Standing on chop you could see the rice field in sunset moments. Awesome.

reviews.author: Tomtomba
reviews.title: Breathtaking views
reviews.content: We didnt see much of the cave itself (tiger cave), but spent a large amount of time at the top of the hill until the sun set. Amazing views, quiet, and very peacefull spot.Defintely a must see here in Ninh Binh!Useful info:Bike and motorbike parking for 5,000 vnd100,000 vnd charge at the gate

reviews.author: Neta P
reviews.title: Cold waters, good views
reviews.content: Came here with 4,5 year olds. The cave is small only if you don't go in the water. Bring a suite and go in. There is a submerged walkway and lights and you can go quite deep into the mountain. Kids were happy to climb the steps. Bring lots of water and large hats / umbrella. Save the cave for last for a refreshing swim after the hot climb.

reviews.author: Katarina B
reviews.title: Nice views
reviews.content: Some quite nice views of the surrounding countryside, although you also get views of sprawling Ninh Binh city. I got there at about 930 on a Sunday in September, so it was quite busy and it got really hot quite fast. There's not much shade, so bring a hat and/or umbrella, and plenty of water (or you can buy cold drinks at the bottom of the stairs for 20,000 dong). While it's not very high, it is a fairly steep climb with quite tall steps. Quite a few visitors were blasting k-pop from portable speakers as they climbed so it wasn't the most tranquil experience - perhaps would be more ideal to go on a weekday when it's likely a bit quieter? Overall, it was a nice sightseeing attraction - but I would have enjoyed it much more if I'd arrived at opening time (7am) instead of later in the morning.

reviews.author: Giles C
reviews.title: The caves were disappointing but the views were AMAZING!!
reviews.content: A steep 450 step climb to the top of the mountain and you are rewarded with some of the best views we experienced in a country that specialises in great views...The caves were a bit boring, but we'd spent time in Phong Nha so couldn't really compare. Well worth the visit (and the effort).

reviews.author: Peter L
reviews.title: The view!
reviews.content: Beautiful view from the top. Climbing the stairs took around 15 minutes.  Little bit crowdy up there.

reviews.author: Travel2006beach
reviews.title: Easy to climb
reviews.content: Felt a bit difficult at first but I made it as the area is small. View is nice. It was 2nd week of Sept and it rained before 5pm. Entrance fee 100,000 VND.

reviews.author: ClaireBrianNZ
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: With a busy day planned, we nearly decided to miss this as it was just so sunny and hot that I wasn't sure I had the energy.  However, with plenty of fluid and taking it slowly we made it up to the top up the steep steps.  Views were great all the way but not much shade.  View from top was awesome and don't forget the last little climb at the end to see where the dragon is.  Definitely worth doing and really enjoyed it despite the heat.  Would be a lot easier on a cooler day, but then the nice clear skies give you the best views.

reviews.author: lockettorres
reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.content: This is not really a cave. You go to climb the karst/mountain and see the views which are spectacular. The climb itself isn't that difficult, around 350 stairs to the top. However, if it is hot and humid (very likely) then it is hot work and if you're like me, 'an ordinary' Brit, you'll sweat buckets. (The Vietnamese seem to go up and down and look as fresh as daisies ... how do they do it?) The views are definitely worth it though. It cost 100,000 VND per adult to enter this and you pay around 10,000 VND per person to have them look after the bikes.

reviews.author: nataliebirt5
reviews.title: Mua caves
reviews.content: Not much to see in the way of caves but we came here to do the ancient 500 stepsMy partner and I have a good level of fitness and found these ok to climbThe heat got in our way but stopped a few times to take magnificent pictures snd wipe the sweat awayWould recommend doing this in the earliest part of the day yo avoid the heat Stunning viewsGardens surrounding peacefulHighly recommend if you enjoy a challenge

reviews.author: Roey K
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: Great views. The climb to the top is tough especially when its hot. I dont know if we got ripped off but we paid 100k each to enter (way too much). Still we enjoyed the ride and sights (get there by bicycle or motorbike!).

reviews.author: Kirsty W
reviews.title: This is a must!
reviews.content: Add this to your list of things to do. It's very high up so the views are breathtaking. It's about 500 steps but you can take your time - easy!You will also see lots of mountain goats on your way up.  Situated in lovely surrounds. Cafe and toilets in area. Wear bug spray!

reviews.author: Jack Zwanenburg
reviews.title: Awesome view
reviews.content: After climbing more than 400 steps the view at the Tam Coc valley is breathtaking. Entrance costs 100.000 Dong per person. Worth the effort and money!

reviews.author: Adrian
reviews.title: Amazing view from the rocks!
reviews.content: The hike might be a bit constraining and sweaty but it is worth for the view. I haven't seen such a great view over the land of Vietnam anywhere else. The hike and the scenery are just breathtaking.

reviews.author: Alex V
reviews.title: Best view of Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Climbing up the 486 steps can be challenging on a humid and hot summer day, but its totally worth it making it to the top. The panoramic views and the pictures with the dragon pay up every drop of sweat. Take water with you as the gazebo with refreshments is under construction. Also, a spare camera battery would come in handy as you`ll take lots of pictures.

reviews.author: Martine S
reviews.title: Great view
reviews.content: Cloudy morning which made the streep hike do-able. Great view once you're on the top!We went early and saw just few tourists!

reviews.author: Matty H
reviews.title: Cool Spot
reviews.content: This is well worth a visit, but be prepared to climb the 500 stairs to the top. In the heat of the afternoon sun, it's a killer, but the views from the top are stunning! There are a couple of stalls at the bottom of the stairs, beside the caves, so you can hydrate/rehydrate after your climb.

reviews.author: Jacky D
reviews.title: Splendid climb
reviews.content: I still can't figure out why it's called "Mua caves", but it was a nice climb up one of these many rocky formations that you can see in the area. It's all stairs to the top, a little steep for the older or younger ones, but our group comprised little ones from the age of 9 as well as seniors at 60+, and almost everyone made it. It was totally worth the view !

reviews.author: Ollie S
reviews.title: Worth it.
reviews.content: We counted the steps, unless we lost count up to the main pagoda there seemed to be a little less, 484 give a few haha  Regardless of this the journey to the top, although tiring especially for a smoker, is definitely worth it. The view was stunning. You can get almost 360 degree views from the top, of rice fields, limestone karsts and Ninh Binh below. Theres plenty of good photo opportunities.  Theres also a second set of steps around 100 to a different peak with equally as good views. If you had to choose between Mua Caves and the Bich Dong Pagoda, I'd say go for this one, there's a little more wow factor.

reviews.author: GuideViet21
reviews.title: Top of Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Get over 500 hundreds steps you guys got to see over view of Tam Cock river and Trang An complex. With the huge lying dragon on top such as coolest place with stunning view. Tickets quiet much 100k/paxYou got free park in that place but someone might stop you before you get there and if you park there you might pay :)

reviews.author: Kristen L
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: Caves are mediocre but the climb up the 400+ steps are absolutely worth it. Go in the early morning or around 5pm to avoid the heat.

reviews.author: PuysPam
reviews.title: Worth it!
reviews.content: We rented a bike coz it was 6km away from our hostel. It was worth every step. The view on top was priceless. Must see in Vietnam!

reviews.author: Kanaena
reviews.title: What a view!
reviews.content: Yep, its a steep climb and 500 steps but I promise you its not so bad once you get started. Its also neat to see Vietnamese couples do their wedding photos on such a steep spot. The view from the top is great you get to see the rice fields/limestone mountains all around and also the boats that are rowed from tam coc.

reviews.author: Eline W
reviews.title: Good view, couldn't find the cave
reviews.content: They charge you for parking your bicycle (5000 dong) and we were charged 100k dong for entrance. I belive we got overcharged. Cave cannot be found, there is only one cave (which is blown out by dynamite) with a lot of chairs and tables (I assume it must be some kind of restaurant. However, you can climb up to a viewpoint which has good views! Recoomend doing so if you don't mind paying 100k dong.

reviews.author: RalphM1968
reviews.title: Take the 500 steps; you will be rewarded
reviews.content: Stunning view on the top. When it is not cloudy 😃Caves are not that interesting though. It s all about the climb

reviews.author: Raymond W
reviews.title: Up You Go
reviews.content: The small cave here is not really the highlight. The best part is climbing up the (very steep) stairs for commanding views of the lovely karst landscape that is the Ninh Binh world heritage site.Entrance is 100k and includes parking. Don't be fooled by the people flagging you down for paid parking.

reviews.author: Sam T
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: We staying at the hotel at mua cave so we get free entry to the top Recommend visit early morning or later in day to avoid to heat.Bring water with you . It may take around 30mins to climb on top.The view is amazing

reviews.author: Anja P
reviews.title: Magnificent... you'll never forget this view!
reviews.content: Don't be discouraged by the stairs. It's not as bad as some make it out to be. Perhaps if you run it! Take your time, and don't rush. Enjoy the wind, drizzle and views. It's so gorgeous out here. Honestly one of the highlights during our whole trip. Entrance is 100,000d. Completely worth it! There's a gorgeous Spring to the right of the stairs for a cool down after if you'd like! Pretty mysterious too. Don't miss this during your stay, it's spectacular! Spend about 1.5hours here 😱

reviews.author: Monique v
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: 460 steps takes you to a beaufitul view. The entrance fee is 100.000VND.The steps have some uneven heights which makes it heavier when you reach the summit of the mountain. Some stepstones are a bit loose.

reviews.author: Fiona S
reviews.title: One of my favorite stops in Ninh Binh!
reviews.content: We rode our bikes from our hotel in Tam Coc (Chez Loan) about 20-30 minutes to Hang Mua. While we didn't venture into the caves, we did hike up the mountain. While there are quite a lot of steps, the view from the top is certainly worth it! (Tip for parking bikes- don't stop until you've gone through the entry gate. There you'll find free bike parking. There will be people trying to flag you down outside of the entry to park your bike for a little money....which at the end of the day isn't much at all so it's not a big loss)

reviews.author: SMSands
reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.content: The view from the top of Dragon Mountain was amazing - definitely worth the trek, but be sure to have some level of fitness, appropriate shoes, and bring some water with you.  The little gardens in the area are lovely and be sure to look around as you'll see dragons and temples in the mountains.We really loved that we could cycle through the countryside to get here - that itself was just magical as you really get to understand that this area is "HaLong Bay on the land".Bring some cash to buy extra drinks and ice cream on the way out - and to pay them guards to look after your bike (they give you a ticket).

reviews.author: Hải Yến P
reviews.title: Very relaxing with best views in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Best view in Ninh Binh and the quite environment was very great. Strongly recommended after long days of working. Good for exercise. The restaurant down there at the hill bottom was great with Vietnamese food.

reviews.author: Elo L
reviews.title: Good climb for great view
reviews.content: Worth the 450steps for the view you get at the top.Make sure you have some baskets  and some water.Just mind the steps its pretty high

reviews.author: Go V
reviews.title: beautiful cave, good view
reviews.content: If you visit Ninh Binh. Please take your time to visit this place, good view to see all city and Tam Coc, one of the most beautiful cave in Ninh Binh.

reviews.author: Escape719207
reviews.title: Worth it!!!
reviews.content: Recommended by one of my friends, read the reviews and photos, and it's way more than expected! Not commercialized yet but a bit croweded during weekends. Pick a rainy day or a sunny day if u want a good picture. Nice restaurant down the hill to try w local food.

reviews.author: Carola B
reviews.title: The top of the mountain is the highlight, not the caves
reviews.content: The caves are tiny and not very exciting. But bring a lot of water and some bananas and climb to the top of Lying Dragon mountain and you'll be rewarded with stunning views of Ninh Binh town on one side and the mountains and the river on the other.Also, for some relaxation afterward, go to Mua Cave and enjoy a drink in the shade with a view of the river and fields.

reviews.author: JanNZ56
reviews.title: Worth the climb
reviews.content: Amazing view make the effort to get here and don't miss the Pearl spring cave at the bottom. Quite expensive at 100,000 entrance and 15,000 to park a motor bike but it was a highlight to look down at the Tam Coc boats

reviews.author: DaniloNano
reviews.title: Very nice panoramic view
reviews.content: The view was worth the 400 steps up hill climb. The good thing is that you can go anytime. The sunlight will not compromise your photos at any time of the day

reviews.author: Fiach B
reviews.title: Absolutely amazing views.
reviews.content: This was when I realised I was in a Vietnamese tourism picture. The views from the top of the 500 steps are incredible. It's not too crowded and it was so nice to sit and talk to others at the top. You could see for miles. My legs were jelly going back down but worth it.

reviews.author: Pita
reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.content: This is a must see! It's very majestic and very beautiful for a sunset watch. The views are amazing and you get a 360° from the top of the cave. It's a bit of a hike but so worth it. Bring your water, a towel,  then rest and take in the beauty at the top.

reviews.author: Nikiesha M
reviews.title: A must see
reviews.content: The caves aren't that great, it's the 500+ step climb to the top that makes this place amazing, the views are breathtaking. Honestly the pictures don't do it justice.

reviews.author: Buiduong
reviews.title: Amazing cave in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: This cave seems to be lesstouristic than Tam Coc cave. Inside this area, there is Mua ecolodge accommodation, this one is wonderful and nice decor. There are various outdoor activities to enjoy and ton of opportunities to selfie and take photo of panorama view of this place.

reviews.author: LauraEvans88
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: Our first stop on a bike ride of the area. 500 steps up to the top is tough. We took a few breaks along the way. Once you get there the view is great and totally worth the effort.

reviews.author: CHH-pretoria
reviews.title: Stunning view from the summit
reviews.content: We did not visits the caves but climbed to the summit for the stunning views. We are not particularly fit but managed the climb ok. Absolutely beautiful vistas, well worth it. go early while it is cool.

reviews.author: DenizM
reviews.title: Stunning views
reviews.content: The view from the top is well worth the steps along the way. Make sure to have enough water with you. Also before climbing up or after going down make sure to visit the cave which is past the steps. There is a small lake inside where you can actually swim. The water is quite cold though. If you are lucky, you will not come across any loud group.

reviews.author: Natalie L
reviews.title: A must visit place in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: You can climb about five steps to the montain peak, and see the view of Trang An( or Tam Coc?).     You can go into a cave, and take off your shoes, and put your nake feet into the cool water.    The taxi fee from the Ninh Binh city to here is about VND 200,000 per trip ( about USD 9). In the park, they sell some water bottles and some Vietnamese style food.

reviews.author: Katherine S
reviews.title: Amazing View
reviews.content: Easily one of my favorite things I did in Vietnam.  The views are unbelievable. Go as early as possible to avoid the heat.  We only saw 2 other people there in the morning.

reviews.author: Candy C
reviews.title: Overview of Ninh Binh
reviews.content: This cave near Tam Coc, you can hire bicycle - about 4 Km. Should come in early morning to see sunrise of late afternoon to take beautiful pictures of sunset. Entrance fee to this place 100.000 VND

reviews.author: Ha P
reviews.title: Best place to visit in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Before going to Ninh Binh, I was told a lot about this peak and also from the research online, the pictures taken from the peak are breathtaking. We rented a motorbike and the ride was about 10mins from our hostel. The entrance ticket is 100.000vnd, also the parking fee for motorbike is 10.000vnd and for bicycle is 5.000vnd which I think it's overpriced. And the parking area is right outside the gate. We climbed 500 steps to the top and to get the best view, scramble up the dragon. Personally, the view is worth all the effort. If you are traveling during the summer month and planning to visit this site, try to do early in the morning or late afternoon, trust me, you don't want to climb up those big steps when the sun is directly overhead. Sun in this area can be quite harsh.

reviews.author: binvinnie
reviews.title: Caves???? View however was amazing
reviews.content: We came here to see the caves. Umm....what caves? Well there were 2 but they are having some work done on them and there's not much too see.What is amazing is the view from the stop of the stairs going up the side of one of the hills. It's a pretty solid walk up, so take plenty of water and good shoes.Also you can park inside the premises for free so don't be scammed and park at one of the two paid parking lots outside. We had read about this scam on Trip Advisor before heading here.It's definitely with a visit if you want a great view of the areaIt's not presently a place to visit if you're going to see the caves.

reviews.author: traceadventures
reviews.title: Skip the cave, climb the 500 steps
reviews.content: This cave is nothing to write home about but visiting the location will enable you to have access to the 500 steps up to the temple on the top of the mountain with magnificent views across the valley below on one side towards Ninh Binh and the Tam Coc valley (where the boat ride passes through) on the other.The climb up and down should only take an hour (we did it at a slow pace in 35 degree heat). Opens at 7am.

reviews.author: Huy Tuấn N
reviews.title: Greatest view in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Compared to Trang An and Tam Coc, this place has the best view after climbing 500 steps to the top. The ticket is 100,000VND quite cheap and pretty lower than other places.

reviews.author: Giang C
reviews.title: I'm on top of Ninh Binh
reviews.content: It's undoubted that the top of Mua Cave owning the best view Ninh Binh where I did take a lot of cool and deep photos.

reviews.author: Jamie W
reviews.title: Hard walk on a hot day, nice view, average cave
reviews.content: We went for the exercise and a few nice photo's because we had a spare day in Ninh Binh.Be aware that there is free parking inside, a lady will try to wave you down and say you have to pay 10,000 but every little can help.Take water and give yourself 1-2 hours for the walk up, appreciation time and the descent.10 min drive by motorbike from queen hotel.

reviews.author: Caroline A
reviews.title: Lovely views
reviews.content: Caves underwhelming, main attraction is the pagodas sitting atop the karst. Entry was 100k dong per person, with free bike parking inside. We went in the afternoon, thinking we might stay for sunset, and would recommend doing this due to the 500 or so steps being shaded at this time of day. It was a very humid day which made it a reasonably strenuous climb. Views from the top were stunning- karsts and rice paddies with locals working the fields. We didn't stay for sunset as it was clear that the setting sun would be hidden by a karst- we cycled back through rice paddies and got a much better view.Definitely do this if you visit tam coc.

reviews.author: Quynh Anh N
reviews.title: Great view
reviews.content: after so many steps to the peaks, we really admire of the great view, staying here, you can see bout Trang An and Tam Coc

reviews.author: Eeva P
reviews.title: "Cave"?
reviews.content: Nice view on the top but maybe not worth the entrance fee (200 000VND). The "cave" was a big disapointment.

reviews.author: annachap1
reviews.title: Great views
reviews.content: An easy drive to get to from the centre of town on bicycle or scooter. It's not an easy climb to the top, but the views are worth it. Take loads of water! The cave at the base has a cafe inside, and drinks are a reasonable price. The cave was amazing- the the climbs were!

reviews.author: TravellingRobarama
reviews.title: Unbelievable View and Architecture
reviews.content: When my friends and I arrived in Ninh Binh we researched the best things to see in the area. Once I seen photos of the Mua caves I knew it was my most anticipated part of our time here! I was sold on the fact that a dragon statue spans the peak of Hang Mua, like something out of the Lord of the Rings! Due to running out of time on our first day, and a train I had to catch at 10:30 the next day, it was beginning to look like I wouldn't be able to fit Mua caves into my schedule. However I woke up at 6am and biked the 20 minute drive to Hang Mua, on the off chance I would be permitted to climb even though they didn't open until 7am. I arrived at 6.30 and the staff greeted me, advised me where to park my bike and then processed my payment, they were more than happy for me to climb even though It was 30 minutes before they opened. The climb wasn't so difficult, i was out of breath but you don't need to be an athlete to do it! Once up there are 2 peaks, one is slightly smaller than the other, from here you get excellent views of the dragon, sprawled across the adjacent peak, from the other the views of the landscape around is phenomenal, I got a picture with the dragon because I was so impressed (any Lord of the Rings or Harry Potter fans, this is a MUST SEE) I felt like I was in Middle Earth! I made it up and down in about 40 minutes. Take water and don't be put off by the price, 100,000 dong (£3.50 or $5 USD) but parking is free and the view is spectacular! The caves are nothing special but kind of cool, but the view will not disappoint!

reviews.author: Fearless641688
reviews.title: Energetic but worth it!
reviews.content: The climb up the steps is immense and seems to take a lifetime, but once you get to the top....... OMG, the views are incredible!Make sure you are prepared and have plenty of water to hand.  There's a cafe st the bottom to stock up if needed.Was a little hard to find, but a real gem of a place.Ooh, and spray up, there were a few mossies chomping around!

reviews.author: I_wander_asia
reviews.title: Great panoramic views
reviews.content: We thought 100,000 dong per person was a quite expensive just for a viewpoint but once you get up there it's really worth it. It will be the best you do in Tam Coc. The name is quite misleading because the cave at the bottom is really not so good but the highlight is the climb up to the top. The views are stunning. The climb up the 500 stairs is difficult but it doesn't take long. Bring water. You get to see a full panoramic view but there are two paths to take. I would highly recommend coming here. It's worth the money.

reviews.author: AaronAikWeiJian
reviews.title: Direct trek up to the top via <500 steps
reviews.content: Panoramic view of the Ninh Binh area, with an entrance fee of 100,000VND. You get to see 2 views, one with the entire area of Ninh Binh and on the other side, the mountains with the some rice fields and a river, which you may occasionally see a boat rowing through.

reviews.author: Marcin K
reviews.title: Beautiful views from top of the hill.
reviews.content: Name might be misleading as climbing the hill is the biggest attraction not the caves themselves. Caves are nothing special but the view from the top is definitively worth a visit.

reviews.author: CrGaBr
reviews.title: Best place in Tam Coc!
reviews.content: Much better than taking a boat around the river and the rice fields. Price is 100.000VND and the view from the top is totally worth the climb.PS: Ignore the guy just before the entrance telling you have to park at the parking. You can go inside and park there for free before getting your ticket!

reviews.author: Simone M
reviews.title: Ok if you have time
reviews.content: Nice view from the top but you might skip if your program is short. I did on a cloudy day and was fine even if the steps are all different. It can be too hard on a sunny day

reviews.author: Lucym1905
reviews.title: Tough climb but worth the view
reviews.content: Ita about 500 steps to the temple at the top of Mua caves so it is quite tough going in the heat but do-able. Make sure you have lots of water! The view from the top is beautiful, over tam coc park and some of the small villages set amongst the karsts. The temple itself isnt anything special although the dragon is nice!It costs 100,000vnd to get in and it is easily reached by bike from Tam Coc. DO NOT be lured into one of the parking stalls on the approach to the gate, we were fooled by a man in uniform ushering us in and we paid for bike parking, to then find out that parking is free past the ticket booth.

reviews.author: Vu N
reviews.title: What a view!
reviews.content: The view is indescribable. I only got up halfway to the top because there were no hand rails and I get vertigo.My family went all the way to the top. I would definitely say not for the faint-hearted, it's dangerous even for the experienced. The stairs are loose rock at times and steep of course, so not best for small kids. We went with out 9 and 11 year old and it was nerve racking.The view however I will never ever forget.

reviews.author: Bettyngu
reviews.title: Great exercise up the mountain and rewarded with amazing view
reviews.content: Stop at mua caves after visiting trang an. It's a steep climb up the stairs but soon rewarded with amazing views of ninh binh. As for the caves...not much of a anything. It will be the views up at the mountain which is the attraction.

reviews.author: chasemarta
reviews.title: Amazing View from the top
reviews.content: We finished out our visit to Ninh Binh with a visit to Mua Caves.  We weren't exactly sure what it would be like.  We climbed lots of stairs to get to the top of the mountain.  Passing dragons and servants along the way.  It was a bit of work but the view of Tam Coc and the surrounding areas was magnificent.  When we came home and shared pictures, those of Mua Caves were some of the ones that received the most comments.We strongly recommend visiting the area and climbing to the top.

reviews.author: Jorge M
reviews.title: Great view!
reviews.content: The cave was pretty underwhelming after being in Phong Nha, but after climbing to the top you are rewarded with a great view. The entrance is 100k dong. The guard tried to charge me 150k but then a lady came and charged me 100k as it should. If you are in Ninh Binh this is a great place to visit.

reviews.author: Wafiy H
reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.content: If you are wondering where to get the view of Tam Coc from above, this is the place to go to. Amazing view of the boat ride at Tam Coc. From Tam Coc, if you look carefully, you can see the Dragon on top of the hill, and thought perhaps it's a private property, but it isn't. A 15 minutes climb would get you one of the most wonderful experience while in Ninh Binh. 100,000 VND entrance ticket, free parking and it's worth a visit!

reviews.author: Steven S
reviews.title: Cannot beat the view
reviews.content: I came here specifically to climb to the top for the views. Knowing it was going to be a physical challenge I took short breaks on the way up.The views from the top are just like you see on the internet but actually being there is invigorating. Magnificent views.I have a bit of an issue with heights and as there is limited railing/barriers I only stayed for about 15 minutes. Took my pics and I was on my way back down.The steps are steep but if you take your time I think most people can do it. I was determined to do it but my legs were not happy after.I was too tired when I came back down (I had come from walking around Bich Duyen) to walk probably 50m to see the cave but in my defence I had already visited the caves at Phongna. My hotel bed was calling me.

reviews.author: Sam F
reviews.title: Nice view
reviews.content: This place is really beautiful, But if you want to see the sunrise you have to clim the fence because it opens at 7am. Dont skip the caves on the left side of the stairs, it brings you to a nice viewpoint!

reviews.author: Fussel86
reviews.title: great Lookout, Cave not really exciting
reviews.content: If you are looking for a nice Lookout this is the place to go. If you are interested in the Cave you'll be maybe disappointed as it is not very spectacular. In my opinion the View is worth the entrance Fee.

reviews.author: shanejonathon
reviews.title: Most under-rated place in Vietnam!! STUNNING
reviews.content: The look out from this easy walk up a few hundred stairs gives you such a stunning view! Something similar to chae hom in northern Thailand.Ninh binh is so under rated by locals in hanoi purely because it doesn't offer the money that Halong bay does. Do not listen to any tour guide that says one day in ninh binh is enough. 2- 3 days is just nice. It's a DIY place. We stayed at Go ninh binh hostel. Perfect base and very spacious hostel.Drive straight into the gate at the mua caves and park your bike. 100,000VND entrance (well worth it). Do not need to pay for parking by the guys trying to wave you down. You pay enough with your entrance fee!Enjoy!

reviews.author: flavergne
reviews.title: Surprising
reviews.content: After climbing the 462 steps of temple it was nice to find this cave with cold water to walk in.Surprising to find this after just two minutes walk in.This caves visit is a ten minutes one but nice to do.

reviews.author: susiesan1
reviews.title: peace and quiet in Vietnam
reviews.content: We stayed at Mua Cave Ecolodge and did not have to pay extra to climb to the top of the mountain. We went early in the morning before the day tourists arrive. There were only 2 other people there so we had a peaceful and quiet visit.The view is awesome, we got some great pictures. Be sure to wear appropriate footwear as the steps are steep and slippery in places. It is worth the effort to go to the top.

reviews.author: Zac P
reviews.title: Great View! Paying for Parking isn't a scam.
reviews.content: The views are awesome but I did park outside of the park. It's less then a dollar and your supporting somebody whose working for only a few dollars a day.

reviews.author: laurianne2317
reviews.title: Ascension and view are surprising!
reviews.content: Ascension and view are stunning and beatufil even if in March there was too much fog so that we could see the whole valley. Caves are less interesting and price is quite high 100 kVND.

reviews.author: B f
reviews.title: Hang Mua
reviews.content: The Hang Mua (Mua cave) is a very short passage under a rocky mountain. There's nothing special about the cave except for it give you a passage to the other side of the mountain range. It's muddy rice field at the other side prevent you going further.   However, nearby there's a wide stair leading up to the top of a rock mountain, about 200m high. It gives you very good view of the area.

reviews.author: TheRur
reviews.title: Must do in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: It is quite a way up, and steep at times, but absolutely awesome view from the top. We did this our first day and I recommend doing that, as it helps understand the scenery and the area better. We were on scooters, i recommend ignoring the parking touts (even though they look official!) and drive right up through the gate of the entrance, and can park free in there!

reviews.author: RRadical_Travel
reviews.title: MUA CAVE, TAM CÔC, SCAM ALERT
reviews.content: Hi If you are planing on visiting Mua Cave or the viewpoint near it, in Tam Côc be aware that the parking is free. The entrance costs 100k VND it has gone up since last year (20k entrance in December 2016) and you can park your bike just past the main gate. There are some guys trying to hustle people for 20k per bike, don't get fooled and just drive past them.I confronted them once I became aware of the free parking demanding a refund, they jumped out to me with sticks and rocks. Watch out! ;) safe travels!

reviews.author: zalnikor
reviews.title: Lots of steps but worth the view
reviews.content: Close to Tam Coc.A good walk to top,like 500 steps.Take your water.Take it slow and easy.The view is very scenic  of the surrounding area.Worth visiting,you need about 1 hour.

reviews.author: fifi_lacarnivali
reviews.title: gorgeous view from the top!
reviews.content: Mua Caves are an interesting visit. The caves themselves are cool, but not spectacular. What makes the Mua Caves a go to place is the walk to the top for the view! only around five hundred stairs but so worth it!!!

reviews.author: shesgottogo
reviews.title: True happiness at sunset here
reviews.content: Not s much about the caves, more about the steps and watching the sunset from the top. Bring a drink and some warm clothes to sit down there to watch it set (it's chilly because of the wind)

reviews.author: OlafRotterdam
reviews.title: Great views from the top
reviews.content: Entrance is 100.000 dong now but worth it. The cave is not interesting at all but the climb to the pagoda on top is great. Take it easy, take some rest from time to time, take a lot of pictures and enjoy the view from the top wich is stunning on both sides.

reviews.author: Amy B
reviews.title: Beautiful 360 degree view!
reviews.content: It's worth the short hike up the steep stairs! Such an amazing view from there on top of "Lying Dragon"!

reviews.author: mariahajek9
reviews.title: nice view on top
reviews.content: so nice view on the top of the mua mountain,we have climp up 500 step to the top.here we can see beautifull view and relax in sunset,but strong wind

reviews.author: robinw001
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: The Mua caves seem over rated. The view from the top is ok, very expensive at £8 for 2 people. Can see better views for free.

reviews.author: Rhynosoris
reviews.title: Worth the walk!
reviews.content: What a view!Costs 100,000vd per person so it's very reasonable. Free parking inside, don't get suckered into paying for any outside.It's 500 steps, it's steep but it's well worth it!! Views are epic.

reviews.author: CemUlusoy
reviews.title: Must go
reviews.content: Extraordinary view from the top, I didn't see the cave him self because I did see a lot in other places but the top is wonderful...

reviews.author: Andrew V
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Of course this is a must see if you're visiting Ninh Binh and regardless of the time I think there will be many tourists. Bring comfortable shoes, there are a lot of stairs and they are steep - very steep. The view is stunning and it's highly recommended to come here when the sun is setting.

reviews.author: jamessmith94
reviews.title: Fantastic Views from the top
reviews.content: Upon arrival there are about 3 or 4 people who try to usher you into their 'motorbike parking' they charge you 10,000VND, however, if you simply drive past these people and past the entrance gates to the caves you get free parking. the ticket costs about 100,000VND per person to get up to the mountain top temple. The walk up takes about 15 - 20 minutes but is not strenuous if you have a medium level of fitness. There are a few lookouts on the way up that can act as a nice breather. The views from the top were spectacular, even on a heavily foggy day. Definitely worth a trip up.

reviews.author: Suneesh_anand
reviews.title: A good steep climb, worth it
reviews.content: For the magnificient view on top, the climb is totally worth it. Not recomended for aged/toddlers.Steep steps are there towards the end and you can walk near the dragons on the top, but rocky

reviews.author: Marloeskroeze
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: It takes a few steps :) (aprox 500)But with a few breaks/pauzes You can enjoy the amazing views!! Bring some water with You!

reviews.author: isabellelizabeth
reviews.title: Amazing views!
reviews.content: The hard walk up the karst is worth it for amazing views of rice paddies and karsts on one side and the river and more karsts on the other side. The cave was weird and not exciting at all so I'm not sure why the attraction is called mua caves. Best views in Ninh Binh. Entrance 100k.

reviews.author: Rob v
reviews.title: Nice view on Tam Coc!
reviews.content: The Cave itself is not that brilliant, but the trip to the top of the mountain gives magnificient view on the Tam Coc area. Definitely worth the €4!

reviews.author: Hung N
reviews.title: Mua caves is stand for dancing caves
reviews.content: 100.000 vnd fee entrance. Just about 20 minutes to climb up and 20 mins to climb down. The steps are quite hight and spent and lean. But when reach the top that is worth to see the view is stun and fresh. Carefully, the top is small but a lot of people there if you visit on spring that time is Vietnam new year

reviews.author: Kelsie C
reviews.title: Best views in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Climb to the top and catch the sunset after a relaxing boat tour on Tam Coc. The view is sublime. Don't miss out on the caves at the bottom, you can take off your shoes and walk through the shallow waters of the Pearl Springs Cave

reviews.author: narolmya
reviews.title: Little Great Wall of Vietnam
reviews.content: The entrance fee is 100,000vnd (4$/ ticket), and climb about 20 minutes to the summit of cave! If you are the athlete, it does not matter, otherwise you will do the exercise gym! From the top of cave, you can look down at Tam Coc caves, the scenery is more poetic in the summer when the rice field is grown and green, then became yellow, the water is transparent alike a mirror. I spent whole day to recognize here by pictures!Let's see my pictures from the entrance gate to the summit of cave!

reviews.author: Marts_x
reviews.title: Well worth it!
reviews.content: Visited here on a drizzly foggy day, and was very spectacular can only imagine how it would be in a clear day. Having said that the number of tourists was minimal possibly due to weather so that was nice. The stairs to the top are quite steep but totally manageable (legs were sore afterwards) the view is breathtaking 360 degree views, suitable for all ages of moderate ability. Also a few caves here as well. I'll let photos pain the picture.

reviews.author: yeonghaur
reviews.title: Great View from the Top
reviews.content: People come to Mua Cave not for the cave but for the view from the top. It's a short climb (10-15 min) that's not too difficult. The view is stunning from the top. You can see Tam Coc, rice paddies, limestone karsts. Thankfully, it is also not too crowded at the top.Worth a visit.

reviews.author: expatali
reviews.title: Don't go if you aren't into climbing
reviews.content: Well, this may be called "Mua Caves" but it should just be called a lookout point. I'd hardly say there are caves to visit here. There are stairs going up the side of the mountain to a good lookout point, however there are no handrails so if you have an issue with heights (like I do), this should be passed on.

reviews.author: Alexa C
reviews.title: View is great, caves almost non-existent
reviews.content: To say there are caves at Mua Caves is a slight overstatement. There are holes in the wall to walk through, but they look like holes in the wall. There isn't anything special about them. When we were there, they're doing a lot of work on the gardens to make it more of a destination with statues and little foot bridges across a manmade moat and island.The goal of going and paying the admission fee for Mua Caves is the view from the top. You should definitely climb the twenty minutes worth of stairs to the top to see the view. You will see the town and the Tam Coc and Ninh Binh countryside as well as the river that people wind down when they visit Tam Coc.

reviews.author: Krystal W
reviews.title: Cute Easy Hike
reviews.content: If you have some time to kill, this is a great little hike with a nice vantage point at the top. It's paved with stairs and would say is very easy. You will likely run into goats on your trip so keep your eyes peeled.:)

reviews.author: pr_qc
reviews.title: The view at the top of the moutain is beautiful
reviews.content: We rented a motor bike to access the site. We had a bit of trouble finding it initially as with most local map and cities in Vietnam, it is not overly clear and indication are a bit limited. The hike to the summit was well worth the effort for the impressive view (takes about 15-20min...). There is a nice garden and small lake at the bottom of the trail up. The caves were not overly impressive. It takes about 1.5 hours to check the place with time for pictures etc. Best to combine this activity with another place to see like Trang An Grottoes.

reviews.author: Wai Ph'ng Ng
reviews.title: Mini 武當山
reviews.content: The 450 steps up the top definitely feels like a martial art student seeking the mystical sifu that resides up in the mountain. The top feels like Wu Dang mountain where Kung fu began life. Together with my parents who are 70 years old worked our way slowly up the top and was granted a magnificent view of the area littered with karst hills and deep valleys. Every ounce of sweat was worth it. The weather also helped as it was cooling and windy but I imagine it would be must tougher if the trek was made during summer. The view of Tam Coc river meandering into the hill rocks was absolutely amazing

reviews.author: grainnecurtin2
reviews.title: Definitely worth the climb
reviews.content: This was such a peaceful place to visit in the morning. The climb is so worth it for the beautiful views at the top. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Jörg W
reviews.title: Splendid views from the top but caves were mediocre
reviews.content: We went here because of the possibilty to have a great view and that was confirmed. The caves themselves are not worth the efforts.

reviews.author: Sail_Scarlett
reviews.title: Do-able climb to a Lying Dragon
reviews.content: Reading about the steepness of the climb we arrived early to beat the heat (there wasnt any). The climb itself doesn't take that long & the hardest part is the height of some of the steps. Also some are a bit uneven have been hewn out of the rock. But take your time, enjoy the various views at some natural rest stops along the way & you'll be rewarded with a view of the lying dragon & the goddess of peace at the top.

reviews.author: B.j. v Pelt
reviews.title: Spectaculair view!
reviews.content: Although we did not see caves, the view from the top was spectacular! Make sure you go on a sunny day (end of the day for sunset), when it'scloudy, your trip up the 500 steps is less worthwhile.

reviews.author: YnLing Y
reviews.title: 500 Steps
reviews.content: Entrance fee is 100k VND per person. Very near to Tam Coc Boat Ride. Accessible by taxi or bicycle. After climbing the 500 steps, you are rewarded with a magnificent view of Tam Coc river below on one side and the padi fields of Gia Vien on the other side.

reviews.author: Elisabeth Ö
reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.content: For people who likes nature and good views, this is a must do! Really beautiful even when the rice paddies are brown and muddy and the sky is all white. The "500" steps are exhausting but you'll get proud of yourself after climbing them and the view is beautiful long before you reach the top. Lots of goats walking around on the  surrounding mountains.

reviews.author: AnnaCandy
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: I just visit Hang Mua last week. It's around 500 steps and quite tired to go. However, the scenery from the top of mountain is wonderful. You should travel from April to June to see the rice field.

reviews.author: rebecca a
reviews.title: Hard but worth it
reviews.content: You see the stairs from far away, and might think oh no.. i sure did. It is a hard climb of 400+ steps, but worth it when you get to the top, especially if the weather is clear. For us it wasn't, but still a pretty view. The steps are very worn and uneven, both in hight and depth, please be careful when going both up and down! Remember to bring water.There is a pretty little park just before you get up, and the mua caves are quite meh. But might aswell have a peak at then while you're there.

reviews.author: yelahaley
reviews.title: Climb yes, cave no
reviews.content: Two caves we saw bit if a flop 😐 but the view from the top of the stairs was amazing. Would rate you do the climb but the caves didn't appeal to me very much

reviews.author: Thomas
reviews.title: What a viewpoints!
reviews.content: Wow! You can find a few of the best views here. There are some caves aswell, but they're not very big to be honest. The main reason for a visit is the 500 step stairway up. ( well, 481 actually :D ) All the way up there you can see the river flowing with the mountains on each side, and that's a really great view. Just get up there, sit down, have a drink that you brought and just enjoy that view for a while. Beautiful :)

reviews.author: wirtualny_teleport
reviews.title: Great view point
reviews.content: Attraction called Mua Caves is actually more known for the view point on the top of the rock.The way to the top is hard during hot, humid days (20 mins of stones stairs to go up) but the view is worth the effort. You will see the Ninh Binh area and the boats floating around Tam Coc reserve. Great place during the day and around sunset time.After you go down you'll find the cave (on your right from the stairs) where you can walk around without shoes, as the water reaches your knees. We went there biking from the homestay in Tam Coc and it took around 15-20 minutes.

reviews.author: paula a
reviews.title: Hot & botheted
reviews.content: This climb came at the end of a long day. We were absolutely shattered so struggled with the climb & heat BUT worth the view & romantic

reviews.author: Mike D
reviews.title: Muá Wow
reviews.content: I turned up on my scooter down a small dusty road not knowing what to expect. Once I arrive I paid a small fee and then started my walk towards the mountain. From the ground the trail looked very high so I knew i'd be able to take some great photos of Tam Coc and Ninh Binh province. 456 steps later I made it to the top of the Laying Dragon Mountain and wow it was worth it. Go climb this mountain!!

reviews.author: Stefan G
reviews.title: Great view, boring cave
reviews.content: If you are on your way from/to Trang An, this is a place to stop. From the top of the mountain you get an extraordinary view. The Cave itself is not special. So in the end of the day the price of 100.000 VD is compared to other sights far to much.

reviews.author: Victor K
reviews.title: More popular among foreign travelers than local tourist
reviews.content: Múa caves mean Dance caves named for its usage as dance theater thousand years ago when the First Emperor of Vietnam, Dinh Bo Linh built his capital nearby. And the Mountain is called Mua mountain.The caves themselves are nothing particularly impressive but if you are fit enough to climb up about 600-700 high steps that lead to an observation point on Mua Mountain you can enjoy the high view of the beautiful landscape. It is located close to Trang An and is accessible by bycle or a motorbike. You can walk there from Trang An too, just over 1 hr on foot.

reviews.author: Chloe Liying L
reviews.title: One of the best attractions in Ninh Binh
reviews.content: Mua Cave is easily one of the best attractions in Ninh Binh. The 450 steps to the top will enable you to see amazing views. Although the entrance fee of 100000 vnd is quite expensive, it's worth the money!

reviews.author: rioocal
reviews.title: Great View!
reviews.content: The view is fantastic once you reach the top of the stairs, we sat up there for ages enjoying the sunshine, peace and view.BUT: 100,000 to enter and I am not sure what that went towards as the cave at the bottom is not worth it.

reviews.author: Getaway190826
reviews.title: Incredibly bad value for money
reviews.content: If you feel like paying 100000 Dong to climb up some stairs to look at the view then this is the place for you. If you'd rather get value for money then go elsewhere. Unfortunately the place is run by an Eco Lodge that is trying to milk as much money as possible from foreign tourists. Our advice is to skip this one and visit some of the other local sights instead - Trang An Caves (150000 dong), Hoa Lu (40000 dong), Bich Dong (free), Tam Coc Caves (195000 dong) and Thung Nham Bird Park (100000 dong) are all much better value for money.

reviews.author: WestlanderI
reviews.title: View is nice but it is not a must see!
reviews.content: The view on the top of the mountain is nice, but after being in Tam Coc and Trang An nothing new, only from a higher point of view. I think we missed the cave, because the only cave we've seen was a bit of a disappointment!

reviews.author: Drathen F
reviews.title: Stunning viewpoint
reviews.content: Recommended by our hotel for the view point. Wow, definitely worth it! After climbing up the 500 odd stairs and reaching the peak, we got a 360o view of this area with golden rice fields, stunning valleys, beautiful mountains and lovely rivers. However, it’s not easy to reach the case through hundreds of stairs.

reviews.author: cx_1234
reviews.title: pretty good view.
reviews.content: Saw a few people taking wedding shoot here, have no idea how they made it up with the gown. You can also see the boats from Trang An There was one crazy guy who climbed to the back of the dragon. Pretty awesome photo but one misstep and that's it for you.

reviews.author: Jrgn G
reviews.title: Nice view but no surprise
reviews.content: Must see place, but it is just a view wich you pay more then all other attractions on the area. If you want catch the sunset go there around 3u30 in the afternoon. Because of the mountain the sun is quickly gone.

reviews.author: Flippityt
reviews.title: What a view
reviews.content: This is not the easiest place to find by bike but riding through the local villages is also an experience and the local people point you in the right direction. The climb is challenging with the hot weather but keep going there are some great views of the town, surrounding farms and the Tam Coc boat tours. I'd recommend going in the afternoon so that side of the mountain is in the shade and take lots of water to sit and soak in the views at the top.

reviews.author: Nathan H
reviews.title: Every time I step out the door, I'm amazed.
reviews.content: Two couples, us with a 4 yr and a 1 yr old, them with a 2 yr old. We got 2 cabins, a large and a small one. The cabins are comfortable (although the large one has a nearly unusable shower, due to the shower head being too low and only able to point directly down) and have plenty of room. The staff are extremely accommodating, including taking me on a scooter to get medicine in town for my son. They really went out of their way to he helpful. But a big part of this place's appeal is the scenery. And oh, my god, the scenery. Not just the mountains and the caves and the rivers and the rice fields, but the hotel grounds themselves are like the magical kingdom Disneyland tries to be. I gave it my all, but no pictures could do this place justice. Highly recommended. Come for the scenery and stay for the people.

reviews.author: brucelovesmango
reviews.title: Good on a clear day, if you're up for some strenuous stairs climbing
reviews.content: The views were pretty nice, walking up was strenuous and at some points felt dangerous because of wet steps. Entrance fee was 100K VND per person, which we felt was quite steeper than the steps for a not particularly well maintained facility.

reviews.author: Silke D
reviews.title: Worth the climb!
reviews.content: About 500 steps up a steep hill. We made a few pit stops along the way up to catch some breath. Once you're up, you have an amazing view of the mountains surrounding you. You can also see the boats below down the Tam Coc river. If you're lucky you can see a mountail goat closeby!

reviews.author: CardiffMaddie
reviews.title: Wonderful views, worth the climb
reviews.content: We didn't actually go in the cave, but instead walked up the many steps to take in the views.  They say it's about 500 steps, it felt like it. We paid 100,000VND entry each, about £5. You pass by picturesque views across rice paddies and then passed a lovely restaurant (Lac Hong) before starting the steps. They have accommodation here. It would be a lovely place to stay. They're building more cabins overlooking the lake, these will be lovely. You begin the climb and almost immediately you see the views across to Ninh Bình. The steps are well laid but a little precarious on times. At the top the views are stunning. There is a little pagoda and a dragon embedded into the jagged rocks. You can climb along it but it is very risky with jagged rocks below.  Well worth the trip. We may even go back at a different time of day. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Hanna-Kaisa L
reviews.title: Fantastic day tour!
reviews.content: Really nice day tour and cool caves to go in just some 100m left of the start of the stairs up to the pagoda.

reviews.author: Alan
reviews.title: Not the caves but the viewpoint
reviews.content: Go here for the viewpoint. Or take water shoes / barefoot yo explore the cave. As it is knee high water. We didnt go to far in but the viewpoint at the top of the stairs is a great 360.

reviews.author: Eric C
reviews.title: Beautiful views!
reviews.content: Worth the walk up the ~500 steps.Beautiful 360 degree views of the area including Tam Coc (which we had seen earlier that day). Well worth it.

reviews.author: tedzeppelin
reviews.title: Amazing views
reviews.content: If you are Ninh Binh, this is a must do. A great hike up the stairs with amazing views the whole way up. If you are in good shape, it is not that hard of a hike and the entire area is peaceful and well done!

reviews.author: Aneta K
reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.content: Climb up the hill it is sooo worth it!!So beaitiful and 360° view.The cave itself is nothing special.

reviews.author: Sarah K
reviews.title: Boring cave, stunning view
reviews.content: We went there by bicycle from Ninh Binh. It was an easy and nice ride. The entrance fee was 100000 VND p.p. The cave is not really exciting, but there are steps up the hill. The way up is exhausting, but you get rewarded with a stunning view. Very recommendable!

reviews.author: natali m
reviews.title: Long climb - beautiful view!
reviews.content: The 500 step climb was easier than we thought and the view is well worth it! At the top there is a nice little covered pagoda where you can sit and catch your breath. Really nice spot!

reviews.author: Martin B
reviews.title: For me not a must do!
reviews.content: We walked there from Tam Coc (around 40 minutes one way). Its a nice walk to the Cave but hot.The entry fee is 100 000 dong/pax. And there is a fee to park your bike. (Not sure about the price)You can see a cave and also walk to the top of a mountain. The cave is not really impressive and only 100 m long and really not worth a visit. The way to the "mountain" is really exhausting because the steps are a bit high and you have to climb 500 of those. I think its not impossible for a untrained and more corpulent person. Just take your time and enough water.The views on the way to the top are nice. For me it was not so impressive. You don't have really an overview of the whole park because one mountain blocks 30% the view(unfortunately on the side where you could have the best view).If you are a budget traveller you can skip this site. The view by bike or motorbike from the ground is much nicer.

reviews.author: emfil
reviews.title: Worth the climb :)
reviews.content: My girlfriend and I climbed the many stairs of Mua around noon time. It was very hot and humid, and to our surprise the climb was shorter than we expected. The view was foggy, but nonetheless beautiful and highly recommended!

reviews.author: Kanliva
reviews.title: Do it!
reviews.content: Do it people! 500 steps or so and you will get a terrific view! You don't need to be an olympic champion to climb to the top. Remember that that you can stop and relax whenever you feel tired. No one will be rushing you.

reviews.author: Amiram P
reviews.title: Great view from the top
reviews.content: We went up the stairs to the viewpoint at the top of the mountain. The view was great and the climb wasn't too hard although it was very very hot and we were sweating like pigs.
